video1
description: African leaders and aviation officials called for immediate cuts to aviation taxes and fuel costs to boost connectivity, trade and economic integration across the continent, speaking at the African Air Transport Convention & Expo 2026 in Lome on Monday.

Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe, President of the Council of Ministers of Togo, warned that policy agreements are 'useless' if citizens remain priced out.

"Opening up African skies is necessary, but an open sky can, in practice, remain difficult to access if airline tickets remain too expensive," Gnassingbe said. "An overpriced ticket <...> is a real barrier for entrepreneurs, tourism and families.”

Rwanda's President Paul Kagame criticised the high taxes and bureaucratic hurdles choking intra-African flight routes.

"Taxes and fees on air travel in Africa are among the highest in the world," he stressed, adding, "A single market works best when rules and standards are predictable and consistent."

Aviation officials noted that lowering prices to achieve true regional connectivity requires tackling energy dependencies and a lack of market competition.

"Apart from Nigeria, which has started to do so thanks to Mr [Aliko] Dangote, we do not produce aviation fuel. Jet fuel is imported," said Abdou Ahabou Idrissou, Director General of the Togo Civil Aviation Authority (ANAC).

The five-day summit, which runs until June 19 under the theme 'One African Sky', aims to move the Single African Air Transport Market (SAATM) from rhetoric to execution, bringing together more than 500 delegates, including transport ministers and airline executives.

description: Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said on Tuesday that Beijing supports the swift restoration of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and is closely monitoring developments surrounding a reported US-Iran Phase One memorandum of understanding.

"The Strait of Hormuz is a waterway used for international navigation, and the early restoration of safe and free passage through the strait serves the interests of all parties. China is willing to maintain communication with relevant countries and the international community," Lin told reporters in Beijing.

"Regarding the issue of Chinese vessels you mentioned, China has been in constant communication with all parties and will continue to make every effort to safeguard the safety of Chinese-owned vessels and Chinese crew members," he added.

The comments came after Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced what he described as a US-Iran peace agreement, claiming it includes an immediate and permanent halt to military operations across multiple fronts, including Lebanon.

US President Donald Trump also said a deal with Iran had been finalised, adding that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen and that the naval blockade on Tehran would be lifted immediately.

Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the memorandum is expected to be formally signed on June 19, with implementation dependent on all sides fulfilling their commitments.

Asked about Lebanon, Lin said the country's sovereignty and territorial integrity must be respected.

"We hope that relevant parties will be cautious in their words and deeds, adhere to peaceful choices, effectively implement ceasefire arrangements, achieve a comprehensive and lasting ceasefire, and create conditions for maintaining peace," he said.

His remarks came after Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz warned that Israeli forces would not withdraw from areas seized in Lebanon and threatened retaliation against any future Iranian attack.

video4
description: Ghanaian Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on Monday announced that the upcoming Next Steps conference, to be held in Accra from June 17-19, will focus on advancing the implementation of United Nations Resolution A/RES/80/250, which recognises the trafficking and racialised enslavement of Africans as the 'gravest crime against humanity'.

"This gathering represents a strategic turning point, an opportunity to transform global consensus into coordinated action," Ablakwa told reporters at a press conference in Accra.

"The objective is clear: to move from recognition to implementation, to move from declaration to frameworks, to move from aspirations to concrete action. This conference will therefore focus not only on what has been achieved, but more importantly, on what comes next," he added.

Participants from the African Union, CARICOM, North America, and Latin America are expected to strengthen coordination in advancing reparatory justice while also engaging European partners on accountability for the transatlantic slave trade.

Ablakwa also highlighted ongoing cooperation with French President Emmanuel Macron.

"What President Macron has also done is to announce that France is willing to work with Ghana to establish a scientific commission on slavery to ensure that reparatory justice is achieved in our lifetime," the minister noted, adding that the French government is ready to engage in the return of artefacts taken during the colonial period.

The UN General Assembly adopted the resolution on March 25, formally designating the transatlantic slave trade and the system of racialised enslavement as crimes against humanity, a position long advocated by Ghana and its partners.

According to organisers, the Accra conference will bring together government officials, regional organisations, and international stakeholders to define practical mechanisms for reparatory justice. Discussions are expected to cover institutional frameworks, cross-regional coordination, historical accountability, and pathways for implementation in the post-resolution phase.

description: Philippine and US forces have held a joint air assault and manoeuvre drill in Cagayan, in the northern Philippines, as part of Exercise Salaknib 2026, a two-phase drill which began in April amid growing China-Taiwan tensions. 

Footage filmed from the operation on June 13 and 15 shows servicemen boarding aircraft - including Chinook, Black Hawk, and Apache helicopters - before deploying for field exercises. US personnel were also captured briefing and guiding their Filipino counterparts throughout the manoeuvres.
 
In addition to the Philippine and US forces, this year's exercise also includes participation from the Japan Ground Self-Defence Force, the Australian Army, and the New Zealand Army. 

The aim of the exercise is to enhance regional coordination and interoperability among these forces. 

The KAMANDAG 10-2026 drills, co-led by the Philippine Marine Corps and the US Marine Corps, will continue until July 1. Following Salaknib 2026, this exercise focuses on coastal and amphibious operations, combining the land, air, and sea capabilities of allied forces. 

According to organisers, the exercise's activities are being conducted across multiple locations nationwide, including Northern and Central Luzon, Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, Manila, and Cavite. 

Military representatives from Australia, Bahrain, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, and Thailand are likewise attending as observers. 
Tensions between Taiwan and China - which regards the island as part of its territory under the One China principle - have escalated in recent months. 

US President Donald Trump said he was putting a potential $14bn arms deal with Taiwan under review, following talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing last month.

description: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has said China places its relations with Nepal in an important position within its neighbourhood diplomacy, during talks in Beijing with Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal.

The trip marks the first high-level visit to China by the new Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) government, following their landmark victory in Nepal’s parliamentary elections earlier this year.

Footage shows Wang Yi and Shisir Khanal shaking hands before they were joined by officials from both countries to sit down for talks.

Wang Yi said China attaches importance to ties with Nepal as part of its wider regional engagement strategy, according to Chinese diplomatic readouts.

The Nepal election brought an end to over a decade of dominance by Nepal's major communist parties, led by KP Sharma Oli and Pushpa Kamal Dahal (Prachanda), who traditionally favoured strong political and economic alignment with Beijing.

The four-day visit follows Khanal’s trip to India earlier in June, outlining the foreign policy priorities of Nepal’s new government.

The meeting comes as China continues to push for closer regional partnerships with neighbouring South Asian states, including Nepal, through diplomatic and economic engagements.

video11
description: Nigerian fashion designer Toyin Lawani is opening a window into the creative process behind some of the country's most talked-about statement outfits. The founder of Tiannah's Place Empire has built a reputation for transforming unexpected materials into high-fashion creations, producing designs that regularly spark debate. 
Footage captured in Lagos on Saturday shows Tiannah's creations, including a dress made of eggs, another made from razor blades and her 'bulls head' headdress design, while designer Toyin Lawani can be seen posing for a photoshoot inside her showroom with some of her many awards on show. 
Lawani says her unconventional approach was not always embraced. “Then when I would create all these artistic ideas, people would literally laugh their heads off, like, 'Oh, why is she doing this? What's she doing? How's she doing this?' I could literally design anything into a dress,” she explained. 
Lawani describes her work as a form of storytelling that extends beyond traditional fashion. “I tell stories with garments. So that's a whole new entity alone. Sculptural garments, edible fashion, editorial fashion, avant garde, ecosystem - just name it,” she continued. 
The designer says originality and empowerment remain central to the Tiannah brand. “What Tiannahs sells to people is you owning your day. Giving them what they have never seen before. I love creating one-of-a-kind pieces. I rarely repeat designs because I want each client to have their own unique experience,” she noted. 
Among her most ambitious creations is a dress made from 10,000 razor blades. Lawani says the design was inspired by personal experiences and the desire to transform something dangerous into something beautiful. 
“So I wanted to create with blades. Something dangerous, but yet so beautiful. And that was what brought the blade dress, because I was cut up a lot, always being cut up, injected. And I just wanted to create, you know, that's a dangerous thing. And it was just a blade that came to me, and I used 10,000 blades,” she noted. 
Her creativity has also generated widespread attention on social media, particularly through her famous bread dress, which Lawani says was designed to help the wearer stand out and turn a single public appearance into a marketing opportunity. 
“People forget that they have just one shot. And that one shot, you can sell yourself to the world so greatly that you will not miss that opportunity. And that was the point I advised her and said, see, I'm working on a bread dress. Wear this bread dress to envisage you have a bakery and put your business in everybody's faces,” she explained. 
Lawani says the public often overlooks the extensive craftsmanship involved in creating such pieces. 
“People don't really see the work that goes behind this," she added. "Do you know how many artisans it takes to make just one? That dress. 500 loaves of bread to even mould a dress. It wasn't ordinary bread.” 
From edible fashion to sculptural garments and elaborate wearable art, Toyin Lawani continues to push the boundaries of fashion design, turning unconventional materials into creations that challenge expectations and keep audiences talking.

video12
description: Ghanaians at the forefront of the fight for reparations for enslaved Africans called for reparatory justice for the continent -ahead of Ghana's global reparations conference  - in an exclusive package from Accra, filmed on Monday.

"Every other race, every other group of people that were harmed and negatively impacted in America, including the Japanese, the Native American, the Jewish people," said Chauncia Willis-Johnson, Ghana Climate Centre of Excellence co-founder. 

"Everyone has received compensation for their suffering, except for African American people, and unfortunately, we know and fully acknowledge that we help build the entire country, so for us to never receive even a discount of any sort on anything, because of our suffering, it makes me angry, and it makes me angry for my son. It makes me angry for his children and his children's children,"  Willis-Johnson added.

The conference takes place on June 17-19 in Accra, and is led by President John Dramani Mahama. It follows the historic UN vote in March. Spearheaded by Ghana and backed by the African Union, the vote declared the transatlantic slave trade ‘gravest crime against humanity’.

But the UN session also split the UN into the Global South and their allies, and the West in a very stark way - particularly over reparations and what they would look like. 

123 countries backed it including all African nations present, and BRICS allies like Russia, China, Brazil, India and many more. Three countries - the US, Israel and Argentina - voted against, and 52 abstained. Notable abstentions included the UK, Ukraine and all 27 European Union nations, who cited varying concerns over the wording and the extent of any 'reparations'. 

“We demand our reparations," Maurice Johnson, the other co-founder of Ghana Climate Centre of Excellence, added. "We're never going to stop fighting for our reparations. This is going to take as long as it's going to take, but if you look at it, if you look at other nations, other people – they've been the Germans, they had to pay reparations to the Jews, and we have had long suffering even until today, and we're due ours. We will not stop fighting until we get our reparations. It may not happen in my lifetime, but it's going to happen."

Tamica Atubga, who served in the US Navy and founded the HOPE Approach, a gender advocacy group, said it wasn't about 'individual payouts'.

"You look back at things like people winning the lottery. There are documentaries and studies that have shown that some of these people win the lottery and win millions of dollars, and then in a couple years they're broke, because just because I have the money doesn't mean that I know what to do with the money, doesn't mean that you know I've gotten the proper education and training to be able to handle the money efficiently, and so I feel like it is important that we do something to heal the countries that have been impacted, and when we're doing that, we have to look at West Africa," Atubga said.

Maurice Cheatham, Vice President of the African American Association of Ghana, spoke about the African diapora around the world - and the need to make it easier for people to return to their original homeland, centuries after enslavement took their ancestors far overseas.

From the 15th century onwards, an estimated 12 to 15 million African people were forcibly transported across the Atlantic and enslaved in the Caribbean, North, Central and South America. 

The transatlantic slave trade was gradually abolished from the early 19th century - but, in the case of the Britain, reparations were actually paid to slave owners rather than those who were freed. £20 million was paid to 46,000 slave owners - 40% of the annual budget - and only paid off in 2015.

description: Nestled deep within the rolling mountains of China's southwest province of Guizhou, the 'Heart of the Earth' lake impresses visitors with its unique heart-shaped lake and blood-red waters. It is rapidly emerging as one of the premier ecotourism destinations in the region.

Footage filmed on Monday captures the lake reflecting the surrounding hills, with its distinctive colour contrasting against the dense forest on the slopes. Tourists can be seen captivated by the beauty of this natural wonder and taking pictures on the bank, admiring the unique scenery.

"What makes it truly special is its colour. There are many famous lakes, like the blue ones in Tibet or the green ones in Xinjiang, but a red lake like this is very rare. That unique colour is the main attraction that brought us here to explore," one of the visitors, Yin Jie, commented.

The lake's striking crimson hue comes from high levels of iron compounds and mineral deposits in the water and surrounding soil. Meanwhile, natural water erosion has shaped the hillsides into terraced rings, creating the view of a beating heart embedded in the earth. 

"You absolutely must bring a drone. You can only truly see the heart shape of the lake from a high-angle aerial view; you can't see it from the ground. While you can take nice photos of the reflections of the trees in the water from the shore, the 'Earth's Heart' pattern requires a drone," Yin noted.

The best time to visit the lake is in early spring and summer, when the water levels are highest and the surrounding greenery is at its most beautiful.

description: Police arrested several protesters outside the Royal Courts of Justice in London on Monday after the Court of Appeal ruled that the UK government's ban on Palestine Action was lawful.

The decision overturned an earlier High Court ruling that found the proscription unlawful, meaning the group's designation under the Terrorism Act remains in force. Campaigners say they will continue to challenge the ban through the courts.

Footage shows demonstrators gathered outside the court as the judgment is relayed over a loudspeaker. Protesters listen to the decision before police move in and detain several people.

Officers are seen surrounding demonstrators carrying placards, including signs reading ‘It's love, not terrorism’ and ‘Saving lives is not terrorism, I support Palestine’.

"This truly is the death of moral law. And all law should be based on moralism. And the ethics and the morals and the desires of the people of this country. It is their ethical duty under their code of conduct to listen to the people of Britain, and to do what is right,” said Dr Leigh Evans, an NHS nurse and medic, as he was led away by police.

Palestine Action activist Lisa Lux read a statement from the group's co-founder, Huda Ammori, who said campaigners would continue fighting the decision.

"We are surprised by today's judgment, after a panel of senior judges of the High Court, including the President of the King's Bench Division, decisively ruled that the government acted unlawfully in proscribing Palestine action, because of the significant interference with the rights of freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. We will fight this all the way."

"We will seek permission to appeal to the Supreme Court, and if need be, take this to the European Court of Human Rights,” she added.

"No matter what happens in that building behind you, no matter what the government says in their declarations, no matter what the home office says in this country, your fight for Palestinian liberation cannot be crushed," noted Sayid, a member of Palestine Action and Defend Our Juries.

The Court of Appeal's decision reversed an earlier High Court ruling and found that the government's proscription of Palestine Action was lawful and proportionate.

The ban was introduced in July 2025 after activists broke into RAF Brize Norton and damaged military aircraft. Membership of, or support for, the group remains a criminal offence under UK terrorism legislation.

Palestine Action says it will seek permission to appeal to the Supreme Court.

description: Hundreds of demonstrators marched through Leipzig on Saturday to protest planned welfare cuts, accusing Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government of shifting the cost of its economic agenda onto ordinary people.

Footage shows protesters walking through the city centre carrying banners that say 'We will not pay for your wars' and 'Your wars and crises are not our burden', among other things, while chanting anti-austerity slogans.

"We are here today because the federal government is planning the biggest cuts to the welfare state and the biggest attacks on workers' conditions in the history of the Federal Republic. We will not accept this," said Chris, a spokesperson for the Verdi trade union, the second-largest trade union in Germany.

"While the rich have continued to get richer for years, the cuts are being made at our expense. We ultimately have to ask ourselves what prosperity actually means. Prosperity means good wages, and prosperity means a strong social safety net," he added.

According to the organisers, more than 1,000 people joined the demonstration, which was held under the slogan 'Enough is enough!' and backed by the Left Party, the Verdi trade union, the Education and Science Workers' Union (GEW), and the Leipzig Stands Together initiative.

Protesters reportedly criticised the government's decision to replace the Burgergeld welfare scheme with the Neue Grundsicherung (New Basic Security) from July 1, 2026.

They argue the new system will make life harder for benefit recipients by cutting payments by up to 30 per cent for non-compliance and ending the 12-month asset-protection period.

It comes as Germany has increased its defence spending following a major legislative change that exempts military spending from federal debt limits. This change has paved the way for a record 108.2 billion EUR (125.29 billion USD) defence budget for 2026, which will be used to systematically modernise the Bundeswehr.

Government officials have argued that budget savings are needed to finance investment in economic growth and national security.

description: The 'world's largest' piggy bank has been painted in the yellow jersey of Colombia's national team, turning the giant landmark in Raquira, Boyaca, into a viral show of support.

Footage released on Monday shows the monumental pig wearing Luis Diaz's number seven shirt. Diaz is one of the leading attacking players in Nestor Lorenzo's squad.

Local resident Andres Felipe Veloza said the idea was inspired by Colombia's qualification for the World Cup.

"As a tribute to them, we painted the jersey on it, the Colombia national team shirt, to support them and encourage them," he explained.

Built by local artisans in 2022, the giant sculpture stands nine metres tall and weighs 30 tonnes. On Saturday, it reportedly overtook a piggy bank in the German city of Ludwigsburg to claim the world record.

Tourists visiting the site expressed their surprise and excitement at seeing the giant pig dressed in Colombia's colours.

"We are super excited that there is such a big pig wearing our jersey just two days before starting with the World Cup, with Colombia's first match," said Colombian visitor Estefany Gimenez.

Images of the enormous pig in the yellow, blue and red shirt quickly spread across social media, turning it into a major attraction for tourists and football fans arriving in Raquira.

Colombia return to the tournament after missing the 2022 World Cup in Qatar. They face Uzbekistan in their first Group K game on Thursday, June 18.

video20
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu hosted Somaliland leader Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi in Jerusalem on Monday, following Abdullahi's arrival in Israel on Sunday for his first official state visit.

Footage shows the politicians greeting and holding talks before participating in a joint presser.

"In Somaliland, everyone has a nickname. My nickname is ‘Irro’. And I think you don't mind if I call you Mr Bibi," Abdullahi told Netanyahu, highlighting historically close ties between Somaliland and Israel.

"I also acknowledge your courage and clarity in engaging with Somaliland, where others were afraid. Your recognition of Somaliland as a peaceful, stable and democratic society in a volatile region, reflecting statesmanship and strategic foresight," he added.

Netanyahu, in his turn, expressed sympathy for the challenges facing Somaliland and referenced Israel's decision to formally recognise the territory's statehood last December.

"We remember as the Jewish people. Yes, [the] small people who asked for the recognition of our rights from the world <...> You're a democratic state. You have a solid identity, and you have the right to be recognised and embraced," he stated.

The two leaders signed a joint declaration to deepen bilateral ties and broaden cooperation, according to local media. Abdullahi also awarded Netanyahu Somaliland's National Medal of Honour in recognition of Israel's decision.

Abdullahi arrived in Jerusalem on Sunday and was received by Israeli President Isaac Herzog. On Monday, he met Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar, who welcomed the opening of a Somaliland embassy in the capital.

On December 26, 2025, Israel officially recognised Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state, becoming the first United Nations member state to do so.

Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991, following the collapse of the central government in Mogadishu, and has since operated as a self-governing territory. However, it remains internationally unrecognised as an independent state by United Nations members besides Israel.

description: In Mexico City, a 'Global Village' has been set up. This space offers food and cultural experiences from 31 of the 48 countries participating in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It is one of the major tourist attractions during the tournament, making it an exciting place to visit.

Footage filmed on Monday captures the variety of stalls where visitors can try dishes from countries including Colombia, the Czech Republic, England, and Denmark. One of the most popular stalls is the Iranian one, where both domestic and international visitors come to support the national team in light of the challenges they face while playing in the United States.

"The world is generally showing a lot of support for the cause of Iranian football. And the thing is, the United States is not only bothering us as Iran," said merchant Seyed Hossein Shegofteh, who is emotionally affected by the restrictions imposed by the North American government on part of the Iranian delegation.

"As a football team, we do feel offended, let's say, in this regard. But the issue is one of general diplomacy in the world that is not being properly respected," the man added.

Other visitors, such as Colombian fan John Chavez, praised the support Mexico has shown to Iran by allowing the team to maintain its training base in the border city of Tijuana during the tournament.

"I think it is fabulous that Mexico opened its doors to Iran, as peoples who live there have similar conditions due to social and economic issues worldwide. So I think it is important that Mexico has given that support and that we, as Colombians, in my case, and as Latin Americans, give it to Iran," he stressed.

Along those lines, Chavez emphasised the cultural nature of football, noting that it is an event for the people and not for large corporations. "All peoples are equal; we live on the same planet. We are not different; we must see each other and live as brothers," the man pointed out.

South Africa's ambassador to Mexico, Beryl Rose Sululu, praised the World Cup opening in Mexico City and its cultural impact. "The opening was spectacular. Mexico was well prepared, and the stadium was beautiful, but the atmosphere was electrifying. I think everyone was excited," she said.

According to the diplomat, the fact that Mexico is one of the three World Cup host venues helps project a different image of the host country. "People will leave with a different view of Mexico. Not the view that Mexicans are only people with drug problems, but they will see that there is a good side," she maintained.

Sululu also mentioned that holding this event represents 'a magnificent opportunity to strengthen ties' between the two countries. "We have always had a good bilateral relationship, so now we will expand it even further. We will promote tourism, the arts, culture, and sports," she said.

With thousands of visitors each day, the Global Village has established itself as a multicultural meeting point where fans of various nationalities take the opportunity to learn about other cultures whose national teams are participating in the world's premier football tournament.

description: US Vice President JD Vance outlined what he said would be included in the US-Iran peace agreement expected to be signed this week, describing it as a 'win-win for the American people' in a recorded speech released on Monday. 
Vance called it a 'great peace deal,' saying it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping while ensuring that Iran never acquires a nuclear weapon. 
"What this deal means is that the Strait of Hormuz is open immediately. You're already seeing oil and gas prices come down just over the past 24 hours," Vance said. 
"Number two, it ensures that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. And we have to back up for a second and appreciate that what the president has done is completely decimated Iran's nuclear programme," he added. 
According to Vance, the agreement presents Iran with two possible paths, emphasising that Tehran could be 'welcomed into the world economy' if it permanently abandons efforts to rebuild its nuclear programme. 
"If, on the other hand, they try to rebuild that nuclear program, they're never going to have the resources in order to do so. It's a win-win for the American people. We ensure Iran doesn't have a nuclear weapon either way," Vance asserted. 
The vice president said the coming months would reveal whether Tehran is willing to dismantle its nuclear programme permanently, adding that the administration wants Iran to prosper economically if it complies with the agreement. 
"Now it's really up to the Iranians," Vance continued, "We're going to see if they're serious about dismantling that program for the long term. If they do, the president has said we want their country to be successful." 
Earlier on Monday, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced that the US and Iran agreed to a 'permanent' and 'immediate' end of the war on all fronts, 'including in Lebanon.' However, Israel has said it is not party to the deal. 
Both Tehran and Washington confirmed that a deal has been made but the contents have not been revealed. Media reports have pointed to a 60-day ceasefire, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to the US naval blockade, sanctions relief for Iran and talks on Iran's nuclear programme. 
Donald Trump posted 'let the oil flow' and said the Strait would open on Friday. Iran's deputy foreign minister, Kazem Gharibabad said talks would continue during a 60-day period to form a wider deal. 
The agreement is set to be formally signed in Switzerland on Friday, June 19.

description: The family of Patnala Suresh, a 44-year-old marine engineer, is mourning his loss after he was killed in a US strike on the Palau-flagged MT Settebello near the Strait of Hormuz on June 10, alongside two other crew members. 
Footage filmed on Sunday shows Suresh's wife, Bhargavi, sitting with her sons at their home in Visakhapatnam, where she scrolls through the last photographs shared by her husband before the attack. 
"[My mind] was completely blocked, because he has been serving in this field for more than 20 years. So far, nothing like this had ever happened. He had not even faced a small injury," Bhargavi said. 
She said she last spoke to her husband the previous evening, when he told her the situation in the region was becoming increasingly worrying after another vessel had been attacked a day earlier, although all crew members on that ship were rescued. 
"First, I got a call from some number saying that he is missing. After nearly one day, they told that he is no more," the widow recalled. 
"After so much pressure from my side, I kept on asking, what is the result? [...] I told [them] why didn't you rescue [him] after so much of time? They told that we didn't, he is no more," she continued. 
Bhargavi said Suresh had spent the previous four months working on routes linked to China because of instability in the Middle East. However, he was later assigned to the MT Settebello. 
According to the family, Suresh had already completed his contract and was waiting to be relieved before returning home. 
"I hope if the US will do any proper investigation, this will be beneficial for three people who died unnecessarily," Bhargavi expressed. "They are not fighting for or against the US, they are not against Iran. They are just doing their job, unexpectedly they became victims." 
Patnala Suresh was among three Indian sailors killed in the June 10 US strike on the MT Settebello; 21 other crew members were rescued. US forces also targeted two additional vessels with Indian crew members during the operation. 
US CENTCOM stated that the vessel was targeted by a "precision munition" to its engine room near the Strait of Hormuz, alleging it was carrying Iranian oil and had failed to "comply with directions from American forces." Meanwhile, the vessel's operator, iOS Marine, denied the claims, stating that the vessel was neither loaded with Iranian oil nor bound for Iran. 
On Sunday, Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that a memorandum of understanding with the US is expected to be signed on June 19, aimed at ending the conflict, including tensions involving Lebanon.

description: Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodriguez, signed a memorandum of understanding with the US company General Electric Vernova (GEV) to establish a recovery plan for the struggling National Electric System (SEN).

The event took place at Miraflores Palace in Caracas on Monday and was attended by John Barrett, charge d'affaires of the United States in Venezuela, and Roger Martella, GEV's corporate director.

"This memorandum of understanding being signed today is also a historic step for Venezuela, so that we may bring recovery to a service as essential to a country's life as the electric service," Rodriguez emphasised.

According to her, this agreement aims to achieve a gradual recovery of electricity generation capacity in both the short and medium terms. "These works will allow us to recover 1,000 megawatts in the first 24 months and, in total over four years, more than 5,000 megawatts necessary for national life as well as for each Venezuelan household," Rodriguez reported.

In her remarks, she also highlighted the agreements in the energy sector that have been made in recent days. "It is very important for the country to know the steps that are being taken. In less than a week we have signed with two companies. Last Friday we signed with the Latin American company IMPSA," Rodriguez detailed.

According to the Venezuelan leader, an agreement was signed with the energy company IMPSA to complete the construction of the long-stalled Tocoma Dam and rehabilitate units at the separate Macagua Dam. The plan will add a total of 2,640 megawatts to the SEN to stabilise the country's supply.

In addition, Rodriguez indicated that the agreement with GEV is not limited to electricity generation since it also includes transmission networks and electrical substations as part of the technological contribution of new technologies for the country.

With these agreements, Venezuela reportedly seeks to accelerate the recovery of the national electric system through a progressive rapprochement with foreign companies, as well as to promote the nation's economic growth.

video27
description: Dozens of mourners gathered in Buenos Aires on Monday to bid farewell to Taty Almeida, president of the Mothers of Plaza de Mayo Founding Line and one of Argentina's most recognisable human rights campaigners, who died on Sunday aged 95.

Footage shows relatives, friends and public figures attending a wake at the headquarters of the Federation of Telephone Workers and Employees of the Argentine Republic (FOETRA), paying tribute to a woman widely regarded as a symbol of the fight for 'Memory, Truth and Justice'.

Family members recalled Almeida's decades-long struggle following the disappearance of her son, Alejandro, during Argentina's last military dictatorship.

"Seeing the headscarves means knowing that mom, as I always say, must already be with my brother, since she did not find him here, surely she is with him," said her daughter, Fabiana Almeida.

She also spoke of one of her mother's deepest sorrows, never discovering what happened to her son.

"The only thing that truly makes me very sad is that mum always said: 'I do not want to die before finding Ale's bones.' And she did not find them. These wretches never spoke and said where they threw him or where he is," she said.

Despite that pain, Fabiana urged supporters to continue the cause that defined Almeida's life.

"Mum always told me: 'Please, we must keep going.' Let us keep going, let us all keep going, please, let us all keep going," she said.

Fabiana also recalled her mother's criticism of President Javier Milei's policies towards human rights organisations, while stressing that Almeida expressed her convictions "with justice, not with hatred."

Among those attending the wake was human rights activist Ines, who summed up Almeida's legacy in a few words. "It was struggle, resistance, memory, truth, justice, dignity," she said.

She added that Almeida's influence would continue to inspire future generations of activists: "She is gone, but her entire legacy remains."

With Almeida's death, Argentina loses one of the most prominent voices in the campaign to preserve the memory of victims of state terrorism. Human rights organisations and relatives say they will continue the fight she championed for more than four decades.

video28
description: An Argentine humanitarian team, which was sent to observe human rights in Bolivia, was expelled before it could start its work on documenting allegations of repression during protests against the government of Rodrigo Paz.

The members were detained by security personnel at El Alto International Airport in La Paz on Monday. They reported that their documents, including passports, were confiscated.
Images released by the mission itself show its members at the airport while Cesar Vilca, one of the delegation members, was separated from the group and detained by Bolivian security officers. Hours later, Vilca was able to reunite with his companions.
From La Paz, the police officers forced the members of the mission to board a plane back to Santa Cruz de la Sierra. They were kept on the aircraft without permission to disembark, and from there they were deported to Ezeiza Airport in Buenos Aires.
Vanina Biasi, a legislator of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and a member of the mission, described the incident on social media as 'extremely serious' and argued that it exposes 'the government's intimidating methods'.
For her part, Ingrid Urrutia, a member of the delegation, said that the incident reinforces the mission's determination to denounce the situation in Bolivia.
"If Rodrigo Paz's government has nothing to hide in relation to the arbitrary, irregular, and illegal detentions and the repression it is carrying out in this country in response to the proposals of the miners and the peasants, then it should allow the humanitarian mission to enter," she said.
The Argentine Foreign Ministry stated that the Bolivian government detected "inconsistencies between the conditions declared for entry into the country and the activities publicly announced by the delegation."
However, preliminary reports have suggested that the decision may be related to social media posts made by some Argentine lawmakers regarding the blockades and their comments on the Bolivian political situation.

video32
description: Colombian presidential candidate Ivan Cepeda announced on Monday that he will file a criminal complaint against rival Abelardo de la Espriella, accusing him of involvement in 'in the looting of the health system' on the Caribbean Coast.

Speaking at a press conference in Barranquilla, Cepeda noted that De la Espriella Lawyers represented the now-defunct Salud Vida EPS in 2018 and alleged that serious irregularities occurred during the process.

"Salud Vida gave Mr de La Espriella a contract for 18 billion pesos, of which three billion pesos were payment of his fees, plus a success fee of 15 billion pesos so that he would defend it or so that he would defend the company in this process," Cepeda alleged.

He said the payments were allegedly made using public or parafiscal health funds. 

Cepeda also claimed that the contract between Salud Vida EPS and De la Espriella Lawyers was signed 11 months after authorities ordered the entity's forced liquidation. At the time, the health provider was carrying negative equity of around 289 million dollars, he said.

"De la Espriella's actions would have had, directly or indirectly, as a consequence that there are 1,600,000 victims of the health system, or rather, of the theft from the health system and of this lawyer's actions," he asserted.

Cepeda said his complaint would accuse De la Espriella of breach of fiduciary duty, private corruption, procedural fraud, embezzlement by appropriation and embezzlement by official misapplication.

According to Cepeda, the alleged offences stem from De la Espriella's role during a period in which Salud Vida EPS members experienced serious disruptions to healthcare services.

The liquidation process of Salud Vida EPS concluded in March 2023 with the legal dissolution of the provider.

The National Health Superintendency ordered the liquidation after identifying serious deficiencies in healthcare provision, insufficient service networks and a financial crisis that authorities said put patients at risk.

video33
description: Hungary's parliament approved the 16th Amendment to the Fundamental Law on Monday, which introduces an eight-year term limit for prime ministers in the first major constitutional reform enacted under the Tisza Party government. 
Lawmakers backed the amendment on Monday by 135 votes to 50, with six abstentions, after first approving a summary amendment package by a similarly large margin. 
Footage shows members of the National Assembly voting on the proposal. The chamber then approved the final unified text, clearing the way for the amendment to be sent to President Tamas Sulyok. 
The package is presented by Prime Minister Peter Magyar's government as a constitutional overhaul designed to dismantle institutions and legal arrangements created during the 16 years of Fidesz rule under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban. 
If implemented as proposed, the measure would prevent Orban, who served a combined 20 years as prime minister across multiple terms, from returning to office. The restriction would also apply to future Tisza governments, including Magyar himself. 
The amendment also restructures the governance of public asset foundations that control universities and other institutions, and abolishes the constitutional basis for the Sovereignty Protection Office - a body established under the previous administration to investigate alleged foreign influence. 
Fidesz and its allies have criticised the measure, saying it is designed to exclude their leader from power. Tisza argues the change is intended to prevent any future concentration of executive authority.

description: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar met Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi in Jerusalem on Monday, after Israel became the first country to formally recognise Somaliland as an independent state. 
Footage shows Sa'ar greeting Abdillahi upon his arriving and posing for photographs before holding a meeting alongside their respective delegations. 
During the talks, Sa'ar welcomed the opening of a Somaliland embassy and said the meeting marked the first public talks between the two sides, following a meeting in October 2025. 
For his part, Abdillahi praised Israel for recognising his country and called for an Israeli embassy to open in Somaliland 'as soon as possible'. 
On December 26, 2025, Israel officially recognised Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state, becoming the first United Nations member state to do so. 
Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991, following the collapse of the central government in Mogadishu, and has since operated as a self-governing territory. However, it remains internationally unrecognised as an independent state by United Nations members besides Israel.

video45
description: A hand-knitted tribute to Argentina's national football team has transformed an ordinary family car into a viral attraction in the coastal city of Mar del Plata.

Footage from Monday shows a Fiat Palio almost entirely wrapped in handmade textile panels in Argentina's sky blue and white colours. A large knitted Sun of May covers the bonnet, while three stars stitched onto the roof celebrate the country's three FIFA World Cup triumphs.

The eye-catching creation was made by 47-year-old weaver Gabriela Soria, who spent over a week producing the cover using around two-and-a-half kilograms of hypoallergenic wool. The design was created using the knitting technique known as 'granny square'.

"It would be nice if it reached the Argentine team, if they gave it a like, at least, so I know it has their approval," Soria said.

Soria has previously applied textile wraps to other vehicles, but said she dedicated this project to the Albiceleste to capture the excitement surrounding the World Cup.

"It has had a good response. I'm getting many messages and calls about the hood to see if I can make it for different vehicles," she added.

The car belongs to her son, Luis Gomez, who said the colourful creation turns heads wherever it goes.

According to Gomez, tourists and locals regularly stop to photograph and film the vehicle as it moves through the city.

video60
description: Despite losing his sight, a Kenyan tailor, Charles Kibe, continues to hone his craft, creating perfectly fitted clothes for his customers and once again proving nothing is impossible in the world. 
Footage filmed at Kibe's tailoring shop in Nairobi on Saturday, shows the blind craftsman engaged in meticulous mending of clients' clothes, using simple adaptations, such as a tape measure with Braille-like markings, for his work. 
"Before then I had many customers, but from then, many customers went away, but few of them remained with me, supporting me, and they were amused with how I was responding to their needs," Kibe shared. 
Damage to his optic nerve caused by glaucoma led to Kibe losing his sight in 2013. Refusing to give up, he kept his vision for the future clear, relying on more than 30 years of experience and his own adaptations to keep his tailoring business going.  
"Two weeks after I lost my sight, I had to look for other ways of innovating my work because I have children to look after and myself, so I had to innovate on how to forge forward," the tailor said. 
His inner strength, impressive skills and persistence have not only allowed Kibe to keep his career alive but also to gain new loyal clients.  
"Initially, when I knew Fundi, I had not trusted his work, but once I brought a piece of cloth and he delivered the work, we built trust and I started bringing my clothes to him," one of Kibe's clients, Esther Njoki, commented. 
The 48-year-old Kibe believes his own example gives strength to people facing a similar situation and inspires them to keep moving forward.  
"What I have seen from when I got sick is the experience of being resilient with your work. I would tell people not to be swayed by their sickness or deviating from what they do," Kibe shared.

description: People from across Hong Kong's diverse communities came together on Saturday for Injera Night, a cultural gathering celebrating Ethiopian and Eritrean cuisine at Africa Centre Hong Kong.

Footage shows attendees sharing meals in the traditional communal style centred around injera - a sourdough flatbread made from teff flour that serves as a foundation of East African dining.

Organisers said the event was designed to use food to bring people together and encourage cultural exchange.

"The idea behind Injera Night is to share a meal as a means of connection. Food, not just in Ethiopia but across the African continent, is a powerful way of bringing communities together," said a programme coordinator, Anesu Ndoro.  

Beyond the food, guests were invited to experience East African culture through music, dance and conversation. Traditional instruments, including drums and kalimbas, provided the soundtrack as attendees danced beneath African national flags.

Ndoro said the centre aims not only to connect African and non-African communities, but also to create a space where Africans from different backgrounds can meet and celebrate their shared heritage.

"We come from many different walks of life, but this is a space where we can come together on equal footing. We all deserve dignity. We all deserve respect," he said. 

Injera Night forms part of Africa Centre Hong Kong's broader mission to promote African culture, challenge stereotypes and foster connections between African communities and locals.

Held every two weeks, the event highlights how food and conversation can create a sense of belonging while introducing more people in Hong Kong to African traditions and voices.

description: Hundreds of children's shoes were laid out in Den Bosch on Sunday during a memorial protest to commemorate children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza. 
Footage shows people gathering around the shoe installation in Market Square as organisers read aloud the names of killed children. Placards with images of slaughtered journalists can also be seen displayed nearby. 
"Since the so-called ceasefire, almost 1,000 Palestinians have been killed," said Esther van der Most, director of the Plant an Olive Tree NGO, which organised the event. "If the Israeli regime is still killing Palestinians every day, how is there a ceasefire?" 
This is the seventeenth such display since Israel's war on Gaza began in 2023. 
Van der Most called out European countries, especially the Dutch government, for what she described as their inaction in stopping Israel. 
"We are calling them out on their complicity. And as people, we are asking to intervene, to put sanctions on the Israeli regime, and to stop murdering Palestinian children, their parents, families, and end this genocide," she asserted. 
At least 986 Palestinians have been killed by Israel and more than 3,130 injured since a US-brokered ceasefire took effect in October 2025. Moreover, 72,996 have been killed and more than 173,245 injured since the beginning of the latest Israeli attacks on the enclave in 2023.

video81
description: Argentine entrepreneurs developed Artrogrip, a protection system for hands and fingers manufactured using 3D printing technology and high-resistance materials, which was used by the goalkeeper of the Argentine national team, Emiliano 'Dibu' Martinez, during his recovery from an injury to his ring finger. 
The protector was designed to safeguard the affected area without limiting the mobility of the world champion goalkeeper in 2022 and current Aston Villa goalkeeper, allowing him to continue training and maintain his competitive rhythm while his rehabilitation progressed. 
Footage filmed on Sunday shows the Artrogrip device being fitted onto a hand, with its flexible design allowing the fingers to move while protecting the injured area. The creators also demonstrate how Artrogrip works and explain the technology behind the invention.
"It works in such a way that you can close your hand, allowing you to grab the ball, do martial arts and so on, while maintaining what we call a semi-claw shape, which means that if you are hit directly, the finger tends to close and not bend backwards," explained Leandro Daniel Ramirez, one of the creators.
The piece was developed with state-of-the-art materials, including thermoplastic polyurethane, a flexible polymer used in 3D printing that offers resistance, elasticity, and comfort. 
The story behind Artrogrip began as a local venture driven by Francisco Francesch and Leandro Daniel Ramirez, who developed a system initially intended to prevent finger injuries in high-performance athletes. 
They shared that their invention reached the Argentine Football Association (AFA) unexpectedly. "After some time of publicising them, the AFA contacted us for the best goalkeeper in the world, 'Dibu' Martinez," recounted Francesch.
He stressed that collaborating with one of the top figures in Argentine football represents recognition for the effort made over the years. 
"'Dibu' Martinez for us is one of our greatest idols, it is a source of pride to be able to help him, even in the smallest way, and an honour to have been able to go to the AFA and help our national team," Francesch shared.
The creators said that after Martinez's case spread, demand for the product increased considerably. 
What began as an initiative developed in a workshop in Mar del Plata ended up in the hands of the Argentine goalkeeper, demonstrating the potential of technology combined with creativity in addressing high-performance sports challenges.

video83
description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog hosted Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi in Jerusalem on Sunday on what both sides described as a landmark visit aimed at deepening emerging diplomatic and strategic ties. 
The meeting focused on regional security challenges and expanding cooperation between Israel and African partners. 
"We both face the threat of radical extremism. We both seek security and stability in the region and in the Horn of Africa," Herzog said during a press conference. 
"Whilst there are those who seek to keep Israel and African nations apart, I am certain these ties will grow and grow," he persisted. 
Herzog also highlighted discussions on trade, industry, and maritime security, with officials and business leaders from both sides participating in the visit. 
President Abdillahi described the meeting as a historic milestone for Somaliland, noting that it is the first official visit by a Somaliland leader to Israel. 
"We are deeply appreciative that the State of Israel has chosen to receive us with such an honour on this historic occasion," he said. 
He added that Somaliland had been seeking international engagement for decades and welcomed growing recognition and dialogue with Israel. 
The visit concluded with a ceremonial toast, a signing of the guest book and a handshake between the two presidents. 
Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 following the collapse of the central government in Mogadishu and has since operated as a self-governing territory. However, it remains internationally unrecognised as an independent state by any United Nations members.

Footage shows a burning car, protesters clashing with security forces, with police deploying water cannons and tear gas. Firefighters were seen dousing multiple fires started during the unrest. Protesters were seen throwing stones and other objects at riot police.

description: The newly opened Huayhuacalle viewpoint has begun attracting domestic and international visitors since opening last week, offering panoramic views of the snow-capped Padreyoc mountain and the Apurimac Canyon, one of the deepest in the world, as part of efforts to boost tourism in southern Peru.

The stone walkway winds along the mountainside above the Apurimac Canyon, featuring multiple observation points and railings overlooking the dramatic landscape.
Located in the district of San Pedro de Cachora, in the province of Abancay, the viewpoint is part of a tourism development project led by the Regional Government of Apurimac.
"Some initiatives from other countries have been adopted, copied, but the geography here in Huayhuacalle also makes it possible for us to build that type of structure in this area," said William Cobarruvias, director of the Regional Directorate of Foreign Trade and Tourism of Apurimac.
According to local media, the viewpoint currently attracts between 150 and 200 visitors per day, with many praising its scenery and resemblance to the Great Wall of China.
"Arriving here and seeing yourself with these views of this wall transports you to China," shared a visitor. 
"The Chinese wall, but not in China, rather here, in Apurimac, in our land, and we invite people to come see that it is a wonder, that they will never forget it again," another tourist echoed. 
The Huayhuacalle viewpoint is part of a group of nine structures that make up the Apurimac Canyon Tourist Circuit. The works have so far required an investment of 15 million soles (4.4 million USD, 3.8 million EUR).

description: A proposed referendum by the right-wing Swiss People's Party to cap Switzerland's population at 10 million has fuelled debate over immigration and population growth, after voters rejected the measure. 
The 'No to a Switzerland with 10 million! (Sustainability Initiative)' proposal would have forced tighter immigration measures if the permanent resident population passes 9.5 million before 2050. 
In interviews filmed on Sunday, some residents argue that Switzerland's border controls have weakened, contributing to higher levels of migration and placing significant strain on local infrastructure, especially in border regions such as Geneva. 
"Switzerland has lost control of immigration, which is no longer what it once was. I myself was an immigrant in the late 1970s, around 1978-1980," said Vincenzo, a resident. 
"There should be limits to how much immigration a country like Switzerland, or any other country, can absorb. Otherwise, it risks becoming a catastrophe," added Gianluca, another immigrant who moved to Geneva in 2014. 
However, others rejected the idea that a fixed population ceiling could solve what they see as a human and economic reality, with one resident describing migrations as a 'normal human practice' 
"There are different perspectives on this issue. On one hand, some people believe that borders should be tightened to ensure security and preserve Swiss culture. On the other hand, Switzerland itself was shaped by people who came here from many different parts of the world," noted Marco. 
"Geneva's highly cosmopolitan character is also one of the things that makes Switzerland special," he emphasised. 
According to media reports, Switzerland's population has grown from 7.3 million in 2002 to 9.1 million. Around 27 percent of residents do not hold Swiss citizenship. 
The referendum was held on Sunday, with Swiss voters rejecting the proposal. Opponents had warned that the initiative could have jeopardised Switzerland's free movement agreement with the European Union.

On April 15, US President Donald Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon. The ceasefire was later extended for three weeks on April 23 following talks hosted by Washington between Lebanese and Israeli officials, before a further 45-day extension was announced in mid-May.

Several West African countries have begun arranging repatriation flights for their citizens, while others have urged their nationals in South Africa to exercise caution amid ongoing tensions.

video127
description: Argentine scientists unveiled Shakajlura riojanensis, a newly identified species of giant predatory reptile that lived around 237 million years ago in what is now La Rioja, offering fresh insight into the ecosystems that existed before the age of the dinosaurs.
Footage filmed on Saturday shows a palaeontologist examining fossil remains recovered from Talampaya National Park, one of the world's most important palaeontological sites, and reconstructing the prehistoric environment once inhabited by the massive predator.
Known as the 'Blessed Lizard of La Rioja' in the Cacan language, Shakajlura riojanensis belongs to the Paracrocodylomorpha, an ancient group related to modern crocodiles. Reaching up to six metres in length, it is believed to have occupied the top of the food chain during its time.
"It would be an ancestor of crocodiles from a group we know as Paracrocodylomorpha," said researcher Ariel Fabian Cardillo, adding, "It predates the first dinosaurs and is particularly important because these fossils are extremely rare in the fossil record."
According to the expert, its discovery and study made it possible to reconstruct what the ecosystem inhabited by this gigantic hunter was like. 
"The habitat was composed mainly of ancestors of mammals, small in size, forms similar to what a present-day fox or a present-day mouse might be. Also other large ancestors of mammals, which were the dicynodonts, which perhaps reached sizes comparable to a present-day bovid, a cow or a pig," Cardillo detailed.
He persisted, "Then came these large-sized forms such as the early Paracrocodylomorpha, as is the case with this specimen, which were the great carnivores of the time."
The scientific significance of the discovery also lies in the extreme rarity of these animals in Argentina's fossil record. The last species from this group described in the country was published in 1997, making Shakajlura riojanensis a particularly important find.

This finding is added as an early discovery in the age of reptiles, just before the era of the dinosaurs began. It predates the first dinosaurs and is particularly important because these fossils are extremely rare in the fossil record." description: Authorities in Bolivia's city of El Alto restarted a medical oxygen generation plant to help ease a critical shortage affecting hospitals in El Alto and neighbouring La Paz, where road blockades have disrupted the supply of essential medical equipment.
The facility, which had been out of operation since November 2025, resumed production this week and began dispatching oxygen cylinders to second- and third-level hospitals treating patients in intensive care units, emergency departments and neonatal wards.
Footage filmed on Saturday shows the plant back in operation as workers prepare and distribute cylinders to hospitals facing dwindling supplies.
The restart was made possible after the municipal government secured the temporary loan of a booster unit, allowing the plant to resume compressing and filling medical oxygen cylinders.
"The truth is that we were very worried, blockades, the city of El Alto and La Paz is completely blocked, [...] and our sick people, our patients, were in very delicate health, that is why we immediately decided to see how to make this important industrial medical oxygen laboratory that we have in El Alto operate," said Eliser Roca, mayor of El Alto.
The plant is expected to produce between 100 and 130 oxygen cylinders a day, providing a vital source of supply as hospitals struggle with shortages caused by transport disruptions.
During the first day of distribution, the cylinders were delivered to several hospitals in the area, prioritising facilities with greater demand for oxygen for intensive care units, neonatology, and emergency care. 
"We are going to supply all five networks, the second- and third-level hospitals. [...] We are reaching Hospital del Sur, the Dutch Hospital, Hospital Corea, and in La Paz we are also reaching the Children's Hospital, the Women's Hospital, Los Andes, in short," the mayor explained. 
The oxygen shortage worsened during recent weeks due to route disruptions that prevented the entry of tankers and cylinders intended for hospitals in La Paz and El Alto. The situation forced public hospitals to declare states of emergency, suspend surgical procedures, and apply rationing measures to preserve care for critical patients. 
According to Bolivia's Ministry of Health and Sports, the region requires between 250 and 270 oxygen cylinders per day, making local production a crucial step toward reducing the current supply shortfall.

description: A portable biosecure unit has been deployed at an Ebola treatment centre in Rwampara. 
Footage filmed on Saturday shows health workers installing the transparent isolation structure and treating a patient. 
“It’s a more secure emergency chamber for epidemics,” said Dr Modet Camara, medical officer at ALIMA in Rwampara. 
“This is a device designed for the safety of the patient and also the safety of the staff. We can monitor patients closely, and families can still see the patient directly despite the isolation measures,” he added. 
Officials from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), who visited the facility, said the chamber represents an important step forward but stressed that major challenges remain. 
“The enormous need that still exists here, both in terms of human resources and logistics and response, means we are really asking for an acceleration of interventions and resource mobilisation,” said Professor Jean-Jacques Nachage, advisory member of Africa CDC. 
“This is truly urgent if we want to contain this epidemic,” he added. 
Dr Richard Kojan pioneered the CUBE in 2010 after seeing far higher Ebola mortality in under-resourced settings than in European hospitals. The portable biosecure treatment unit was designed for rapid deployment in low-resource outbreaks, allowing safer monitoring and treatment. 
The World Health Organisation said that the outbreak had risen to 676 confirmed cases and 136 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with Ituri province accounting for more than 90% of infections. Neighbouring Uganda has also recorded 19 confirmed cases linked to the outbreak. WHO continues to classify the risk inside the DRC as “very high” as the Bundibugyo strain spreads to new health zones.

description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar on Saturday accused Viktor Orban's government of misleading the public over migration policy during a press conference in Budapest. 
He alleged that the previous Fidesz administration was privately preparing migrant reception facilities at a former agricultural school complex in Csermajor while publicly maintaining a hardline anti-migration stance. 
"This daily one million euros, about which, by the way, the minutes of the cabinet meetings acknowledge, not that it is justified, but that the previous government did everything to ensure there would be a penalty of this severity," Magyar stated. 
In June 2024, the European Court of Justice imposed a €200 million lump-sum penalty on Hungary and ordered an additional €1 million-a-day fine for failing to comply with EU asylum rules. 
Magyar said his government was examining approaches used in countries including Poland and Finland in an effort to meet Hungary's EU obligations without establishing migrant camps. 
"We are working to develop such a regulation so that, on the one hand, there indeed won't be migrant camps in Hungary, and we won't have to continue paying this daily fine of one million euros, which is not paid by Viktor Orban and his associates," he continued. 
Asked about the EU Migration and Asylum Pact, Magyar said Hungary would favour the solidarity mechanism's 'third option' of providing technical assistance rather than accepting relocated asylum seekers. 
"There is a third option, for example, which the Orban government also used previously, providing additional technical border protection assistance through Frontex to either Greece or Serbia," he said. 
Magyar argued that the pact extends beyond the solidarity mechanism and includes provisions that are stricter than previous EU migration rules. 
"This is not only about the migration pact. There are a lot of detailed rules involved, and indeed, it tightens the previous migration rules in many aspects," he continued. 
On Friday, the EU implemented a new set of rules governing how its 27 member states handle irregular migration and asylum seekers. 
According to EU officials, the framework introduces mandatory registration, security, and vulnerability checks for people entering the bloc irregularly, while creating faster procedures for processing asylum claims and returns.

video151
description: South Africa’s Deputy Minister of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, Bernice Swartz, led an electronic waste collection drive in Langa on Friday as part of a nationwide awareness campaign highlighting the health and environmental risks posed by discarded household appliances. 
Footage shows residents bringing old appliances and electronic devices to collection points, where recycling companies weigh items before processing them for recovery. Additional scenes show workers dismantling electronics and separating components at a recycling facility, where materials are converted into recycled products. 
Swartz warned that electronic waste remains one of South Africa’s most overlooked environmental challenges, with the vast majority of discarded devices not being disposed of safely. 
“South Africa has 300,000 tonnes of e-waste currently and only 10 percent of it is managed properly,” she said. “Our role is to teach communities that e-waste must not go to landfill sites because we are trying to reach zero waste to landfill.” 
She said many common household items, including refrigerators, microwaves, kettles, irons and toys, contain hazardous substances such as lead and mercury that can pose serious health risks if stored improperly or dumped. 
“Our end goal is for people to understand that waste is gold and that all sorts of waste can be recycled,” Swartz said. “Any waste has a bearing on the air quality we breathe, and South Africans have a constitutional right to an environment that is not harmful to their health and wellbeing.” 
Residents who handed in old electronics at the event received supermarket vouchers or cash incentives as part of efforts to encourage responsible disposal. The government is also working with recycling companies to establish neighbourhood buy-back centres aimed at making recycling more accessible. 
According to the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, South Africa generates around 300,000 tonnes of electronic waste each year. A fraction is processed through formal recycling channels, while the remainder is either stockpiled in homes or sent to landfill sites. 
The campaign forms part of broader efforts to promote a circular economy and support South Africa’s Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations, introduced in 2021 and implemented from 2022. The rules require producers to fund systems for the collection, recycling and recovery of products placed on the market.

description: Indian social worker Sunil Joseph has secured a Guinness World Record for the world's largest collection of paper cups. 
Officially verified in December 2025, the 57-year-old's collection includes 858 unique paper cups from 31 countries, the result of a lifelong passion for collecting unusual items worldwide. 
Footage filmed at Joseph's home in Kerala on Thursday shows him surrounded by rows of paper cups of every shape and size, from small coffee cups to oversized soft-drink containers from global brands. It also shows his extensive mug collection and a wall covered with Guinness World Records certificates. 
Joseph said his fascination with collecting began in childhood and has remained a constant throughout his life. 
"I just collect all these things like stamps, currencies, cups, razor blades, wrappers, lottery tickets, then tea bags and whatever other things, it's something different," he said. 
His attempt to claim the paper cup record began five years ago after a Guinness title he previously held for a collection of 5,986 phone cards, set in 2013, was surpassed. 
"Each and every record has specific rules. This cup, there's no wax. We cannot use any wax or any plastic [...] So, we'll collect, and each cup has specifications, ml, how much they will fill, and there are many, many. Each and every cup, we must write down a description and send it to them," he explained. 
With the paper cup record now secured, Joseph has already turned his attention to another Guinness title, this time for his collection of wedding invitation cards.

Crowds from a range of campaign groups can also be seen listening to updates from inside the courtroom as sentencing was handed down to four activists involved in a raid on an Elbit Systems site in August 2024. 
Campaigners condemned the judge's decision to classify the raid as terrorism-related, arguing the activists were motivated by opposition to Israel's military operations in Gaza. 
"A decision has been made by the judge to include in their sentencing a terrorism connection," said Moazzam Begg, adding, "That means for an ordinary criminal damage conviction, the sentencing can increase by many years."

Samuel Corner received the longest sentence of seven years and eight months, while Charlotte Head and Leona Kamio were both sentenced to five years. Fatema Rajwani was given a sentence of four years and eight months. After their release, all four will serve an additional year on probation.

description: Anna Bezrukova, a 21-year-old up and coming designer from St Petersburg has a passion for a very bizarre form of 'living art' - some truly crazy fashion and art installations made using kombucha, or fermented tea.
Footage from Thursday shows some of her wacky creations - including a pair of underpants and a skeleton - as well as her working with the biomaterial, which starts off as tea and turns into cellulose mats or strips to be fashioned into artworks.
"It is stretchy and flexible," she explained. "If it gets into water or rain, it turns back into kombucha. Then it dries again and keeps its shape. But it becomes soft when wet, so it needs to be stabilised."
The underpants were her very first creation - but she admitted she's yet to find a buyer! Her piece de resistance is a mummified skeleton - which she calls 'The Leader' - complete with tattoos and internal lighting.
"This 'Leader' is a collective image of all humanity, supposedly waiting for resurrection. Light symbolises that the process has already begun, everything has started, but there is still some waiting," she mused.
Anna also enjoys working with other 'living materials'; her own boots are made from bark and she experiments with bioplastics, coffee-based materials, grass, wheat, and plant roots.
Her next step is a full collection of bio-material clothing - and if her early creations are anything to go by, this 'living' artist could very soon be living the dream.

"At my direction, the United States Southern Command delivered a swift and lethal kinetic strike to successfully execute Nino Guerrero, the infamous leader of Tren De Aragua, one of the most bloodthirsty Terrorist Organisations on Planet Earth," Trump wrote.

The strike formed part of Trump's pledge to combat criminals from outside the country, whom he said were able to enter the United States under Joe Biden's tenure. He added that the operation was carried out with the assistance of Venezuelan authorities.

"This action was coordinated closely with our friends in Venezuela, with whom we are working very well. As a result, Tren de Aragua terrorists no longer have a safe haven in Venezuela or anywhere else, and, under my leadership, we will find these vicious murderers and drug lords anytime, anyplace, and send them to the depths of hell where they belong," the US leader said.

No US officials, apart from Trump, had issued any comment on the strike or presented evidence verifying Guerrero's death at the time of publication.

Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, widely known as Nino Guerrero, has long been a priority target for US authorities, and the Trump administration has repeatedly sanctioned him and other Tren de Aragua leaders over alleged involvement in drug trafficking, human trafficking, money laundering and other crimes.

The gang has also been accused of working with Venezuela's former government under Nicolas Maduro.

description: Rene Meulensteen, the assistant manager of the Iraqi football team, dismissed concerns about the team's entry into the United States during an ongoing visa dispute, as the players trained in West Virginia in preparation for their World Cup opening match against Norway.

Footage filmed on Friday shows the team arriving at the Greenbrier Sports Performance Center in White Sulphur Springs prior to training, as media access was restricted and the session was delayed due to a thunderstorm.

"It was fairly smooth. I mean, we got all the all the visas done beforehand <...> It's just a few randomly that people got, you know, questioned for a few other things, which was normal," Meulensteen told reporters.

"There's nothing to do with us. It is obviously security issues that that America has put in place. Everything has been fine now, so no issues there," he continued.

The comments follow reports of multiple teams and fans, especially from the Global South, facing entry challenges to the United States due to ongoing travel restrictions. Iran announced that 15 of its officials were denied visas, while Somali referee Omar Artan was refused entry over 'vetting concerns.

Speaking on Iraq's World Cup preparations - their first qualification in 40 years - Meulensteen expressed excitement for the tournament and emphasised the squad's unity.

"It's the highest platform in football that exists and the purest platform that exists because obviously all the nations have to select the best players of the country. You know, there's no agents involved, there's no transfers involved," he pointed out.

"Togetherness, you know, being a family. And even if you've been born as an Iraqi outside Iraq, you're still representing Iraq with that crest on your chest. And all these people are very, very proud to be together," the manager added.

Iraq are in Group I of the 2026 World Cup alongside France, Senegal and Norway in a challenging draw, opening their campaign against Norway at Gillette Stadium on June 16.
