description: Haitham Al-Ghais, Secretary-General of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) said that Russia and Saudi Arabia play a key role in stabilising global energy markets, speaking during a plenary session at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum on Thursday.
"We at OPEC take pride of our collaboration with Russia, with the Russian Federation, with its authorities in the energy field, in the ministry, and we appreciate the role that the Russian Federation has been playing since 2017, 2016, I beg your pardon, when this agreement was signed in preserving and promoting oil market stability. And we have seen it twice on two, I would say, momentous occasions, both in 2015 and 2016, when we had the first downturn in the oil industry, where Russia played an instrumental role, being also the co-chair of OPEC Plus with Saudi Arabia, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia being the chair. I think the two countries have played a very impactful and very solid role in guiding oil market stability," the head noted.
Saudi Arabia's Energy Minister Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud noted that, despite global instability, oil-exporting countries must demonstrate a responsible approach to the world.
"No matter what severe situation we’re going through, we have to challenge this environment and still continue attending to our own ambitions, because we cannot forfeit the future of the forthcoming generations. And I believe strongly that we have the confidence to demonstrate to people and to everywhere else that we have and shall continue to be a resilient provider of energy at all circumstances ", the minister stated.
For his part, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak highlighted the uncertainty in the global energy sector and economy.
"Global changes in supply chains and global changes in the capacity to transport energy resources force us to consider what will happen tomorrow, and in 5 to 10 years’ time. In other words, the assessments made just a few years ago now need to be radically revised, both from a behavioural perspective and in terms of co-operation between countries, which, in principle, can work together to solve these problems," Novak noted.
The 29th St Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) takes place on June 3-6. More than 20,000 people are set to attend, with politicians from around 76 countries making the journey. 
Since its establishment in 1997, the forum has served as a platform for international dialogue on global economic issues. Vladimir Putin has taken part in the event regularly since 2005.

SOT, Alexander Novak, Russian Deputy Prime Minister (Russian): "The global energy sector is under pressure from a decline in supply. And, of course, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, damage to infrastructure and energy facilities in the Gulf states - all of this is having a significant impact on the reduction in supply today. By general estimates, approximately 12 million barrels a day are not reaching global energy markets. This is a huge amount, representing more than 10 percent - just over 10 percent - of total global supply. And when it comes to global trade, the figure is even higher, because global trade is slightly less than total demand. And this amounts to around 15-17 percent overall, so, of course, these radical changes in supply are shaping new trends today, including in consumer behaviour. Logistics routes are changing; we are seeing a sharp rise in freight rates and a general shortage of tankers to transport energy resources. We can see that prices are rising as a result, and this is all having an impact on global economic growth; indeed, as we have seen, many analysts and agencies have already lowered their global economic growth forecasts for 2026 by 0.3 percent, but I think the figure could be even higher if the conflict drags on. As for inflation, there is also a 0.4 percent rise in average global inflation, which is also a result of rising prices. But most importantly, this affects not only consumers and energy producers - it affects related industries and the economy as a whole. We can see that, down the supply chain, this affects petrochemicals, fertilisers, and rising prices for electricity, housing and utilities. This also impacts food security, as it relates to fertiliser production. Therefore, of course, such tectonic shifts are taking place in the economy, not just in the energy sector. In my opinion, if this situation does indeed persist for a long time, the impact will be significantly more negative for both the energy sector and the economy as a whole, if the conflict continues, because there is a limit to how long the shortfall in supply can be offset by the surplus that existed until recently. Today, we can see that this was a period when demand was low during the winter. Consumers are reducing demand, and we see that many countries have restricted their consumption of energy resources, primarily petroleum products, which are in short supply at present. This also applies to aviation fuel, and we see that flights are being restricted in many countries. All of this, of course, will likely prompt consumers to react to future changes in demand. Most likely, such tectonic shifts will be aimed at seeking new logistics routes, building infrastructure, exploring new ways to transport energy resources, and finding alternatives to them. And this shortfall could be made up by other alternative sources. Consequently, we are currently facing a rather critical situation, which has not yet been quantified in any figures, but this critical mass, in my view, is gradually building up and may, in time, become a more significant factor influencing all processes related to the energy sector and other sectors of the economy. Today we discussed this with our colleagues. We have just held a meeting with His Majesty Abdulaziz Bin Salman. We came to the conclusion that no one knows what the current demand outlook is. In other words, uncertainty has simply multiplied. And this uncertainty is not limited to the energy sector, but extends to the economy as a whole. And, of course, we need to respond to all this, discuss it together and take action, because it affects virtually every country, as well as consumers and producers. Global changes in supply chains and global changes in the capacity to transport energy resources force us to consider what will happen tomorrow, and in 5 to 10 years’ time. In other words, the assessments made just a few years ago now need to be radically revised, both from a behavioural perspective and in terms of co-operation between countries, which, in principle, can work together to solve these problems."
SOT, Aleksandr Dyukov, Gazprom Neft management board chairman (Russian): "We have learnt to work effectively with heterogeneous and thin layers, that is, layers just a few metres thick - 2, 3 or 4 metres - whereas, once again, our colleagues in the Middle East are developing layers tens or even hundreds of metres thick. The unexpected catastrophe has compounded the community's daily challenges, forcing humanitarian workers to navigate logistically difficult conditions to provide basic relief.

video673
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Wednesday that Budapest had reached an agreement with Ukraine to expand minority rights for around 100,000 ethnic Hungarians in the western Transcarpathia region.

"In three weeks, we have managed to achieve what the Orban government could not for many long years <...> I can announce that we have achieved a breakthrough with our Ukrainian negotiating partners regarding the linguistic, educational, and cultural rights of our Hungarian compatriots in Transcarpathia," remarked Magyar in a video address from Paris.

"100,000 Hungarian people are getting back their fundamental rights and the hope that they can pass on to their children the culture and identity they received from their parents and grandparents," he continued.

The deal, according to Magyar, would also secure Budapest's approval to move Ukraine's accession bid forward in the European Union. It would take effect when Ukraine completes the required legal changes and incorporates them into its minority action plan submitted to the bloc.

“The Hungarian government calls on Ukraine to amend its minority action plan as agreed. If this happens, the Hungarian government will agree to the Union opening the first Accession Negotiation Cluster,” he noted.

"In accordance with the principle of equal treatment, a fast-track accession procedure cannot be applied to Ukraine or any other country," Magyar underlined. "If Ukraine is able to close the EU accession negotiations in 10 or 15 years, Hungary will hold a legally binding referendum on the issue."

Opening accession clusters requires the unanimous approval of all 27 EU member states.

Kiev has yet to confirm the deal publicly.

Last month, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz proposed granting Ukraine 'associate member' status, which would allow Ukrainian officials to participate in EU summits and ministerial meetings without holding voting rights.

Albania is currently the frontrunner for EU membership. Ukraine was granted EU candidate status in 2022, and the accession negotiations formally opened in 2025.

description: A Caritas-World Food Programme (WFP) health centre has been launched in Goma to shelter and monitor 87 people from high-risk areas placed under precautionary quarantine as the Ebola outbreak spreads across the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and beyond.

Footage captured on Wednesday shows medical staff preparing and portioning food before delivering it to patients in isolation rooms.

"We consider these people coming from high-risk areas. They must not go directly back to their homes. They must first be put somewhere, housed somewhere to carry out the investigations. And during these 21 days, as the protocol states, they must be assisted," explained nutritionist Fabrice Kabongo.

"We launched this activity last Saturday. In light of the evolving epidemic and the identified needs, the authorities deemed it necessary for the WFP and Caritas to provide care for these individuals. Currently, 87 beneficiaries are receiving food assistance," he added.

Those unable to complete the three-week quarantine were provided with supplies and safety measures to help contain the virus, according to humanitarian emergency coordinator Eddy Yamwenziyo.

"So normally, these people must spend 21 days in quarantine. But since some cannot complete the 21 days, we give the option to even assist them in their respective households in case of discharge… We continue to provide assistance at the household level using food kits provided by the WFP," he noted.

description: Kyrgyzstan secured its first-ever seat on the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday, while Germany suffered a surprise defeat in voting for non-permanent members serving the 2027-2028 term.

"Having obtained the required two-thirds majority and the largest number of votes, Kyrgyzstan is elected as a member of the Security Council for a two-year term beginning on January 1st, 2027," said UN General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock.

"I congratulate the states which have been elected members of the Security Council today, and I thank the tellers for their assistance in this election," she added.

It marks the first time Germany has failed to secure one of the rotating seats.
The UN General Assembly elected Kyrgyzstan, Austria, Portugal, Zimbabwe, and Trinidad and Tobago to serve on the Security Council from January 1, 2027.

Kyrgyzstan won the Asia-Pacific seat after several rounds of voting against the Philippines, securing 142 votes to 49 in the final round and marking a diplomatic milestone for the Central Asian country.

Germany failed to secure one of the two Western European and Others Group seats, receiving 104 votes and falling short of the required two-thirds majority. Portugal and Austria were elected with 134 and 131 votes respectively, ending Berlin’s bid to return to the council despite an active international campaign.

"Obviously, the result is a real disappointment," said German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who blamed Russia and Berlin's ongoing support for Ukraine for the bitter setback.

"It also may have cost us votes that Germany must always assume a special responsibility for Israel with regard to the Middle East conflict," he added.

The result comes at a difficult moment for Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Recent polling has shown that only 16% of Germans are satisfied with his leadership, with support for Germany’s conservative CDU/CSU bloc dwindling. A poll in April found Merz was the most unpopular leader in the world - coming bottom of a poll of 24 democratically elected heads. 

The Security Council is responsible for maintaining international peace and security. It consists of five permanent veto-holding members, China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States, alongside ten elected members serving two-year terms.

The newly elected states will formally begin their mandates on January 1, 2027, replacing Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama and Somalia.

description: As energy prices continue to pressure household and business budgets, a Mozambican startup offers a technological solution aimed at reducing waste and cutting costs.

Footage from Tuesday shows Xiphefu co-founder Jerssen Sengulane demonstrating the company’s technology, remotely controlling lights and air conditioners through a smartphone while working inside the startup’s workshop.

Founded by Sengulane and Nilza Mazive, Xiphefu - meaning 'lamp' in the Changana language - started as a university final-year project and has since transformed into a thriving business. The company creates innovative devices that enable users to remotely monitor and control their electrical equipment anytime, anywhere, using mobile phones or computers.

"The first solution we created was a digital switch," Sengulane explained, adding that the technology enables remote control of appliances such as air conditioners, water pumps and lighting systems while also allowing equipment to operate automatically according to pre-set schedules.

As demand for its services grew, the company developed a second device capable of tracking electricity consumption in real time. "Through the system, users can access their energy consumption readings. We can see how much energy was consumed throughout the month, by day, and even in ten-minute intervals," Sengulane added.

According to man, the monitoring system helps customers identify peak consumption periods and make informed decisions to improve efficiency, while the company also assists clients in analysing the collected data.

Recognising that some users were unfamiliar with technology-based systems, Xiphefu later integrated artificial intelligence with WhatsApp, creating a more accessible platform for customers.

Client Angela Laisse said the system has significantly reduced her household’s electricity use, allowing her to control appliances remotely and optimise air conditioner performance based on room temperature rather than continuous operation.

"In terms of consumption, we have seen a significant reduction. Depending on usage, energy consumption can drop to around 20 to 25 per cent of what it was before," she explained.

Founded in 2016, Xiphefu now serves around 300 customers across Mozambique, positioning itself as one of the country’s leading providers of smart energy management technologies aimed at reducing costs, minimising waste and improving energy efficiency.

The mobilisation coincided with the anniversary of the first Ni Una Menos march, held on June 3, 2015, following the femicide of Chiara Paez, a 14-year-old teenager murdered by her 16-year-old boyfriend in the town of Rufino.

During the protest, some demonstrators played percussion instruments and, through banners, demanded that the Argentine government implement public policies for the prevention and protection of women and girls against gender violence.

According to data released by the Supreme Court of Justice of the Nation at the end of May, Argentina recorded 200 femicide victims in 2025, representing a 12.3 percent decrease compared to the previous year.

Human rights groups and feminist collectives maintain that tackling gender-based violence remains a critical challenge for President Javier Milei, whose administration has sought to remove femicide from the country’s penal code. 

During his 2025 Davos address, Milei criticised the legal classification, arguing it creates an unequal system by effectively ruling that a woman's life is worth more than a man's.

description: Thousands of protesters gathered in Buenos Aires on Wednesday to mark the 11th anniversary of the 'Ni Una Menos' (Not One Woman Less) movement, demanding public policies to combat gender-based violence and femicide.

"The far-right government we are in constantly tries to get us used to living with increasingly higher levels of violence," said Veronica Gago, a member of Ni Una Menos.

"The government of Javier Milei threatens time and again to remove the figure of femicide which, as we always say, is not just a legal category, it is a political category. Because we insist that every femicide is political," added Gago.

Protesters criticised President Javier Milei for seeking to remove femicide from Argentina's penal code, following his 2025 Davos address, where he argued the classification unfairly implies that a woman's life is worth more than a man's.

Soledad Serrano, whose family has been directly impacted, argued that cases have continued to escalate in recent years. 

"It seems to me that the government, by wanting to remove what is the label of femicide, is going backwards," she stated, emphasising that naming the crime is vital to addressing specific violence against women.

Among those demanding accountability was Patricia Ortiz, mother of Micaela Ortiz, who was murdered in 2021. 

Ortiz said there were serious irregularities in the judicial handling of her daughter's case, explaining that she was forced to gather evidence independently to ensure the investigation moved forward.

According to the official registry published by the Supreme Court of Justice at the end of May, Argentina recorded 200 femicide cases in 2025. 

While this represents a 12.3 percent decrease from the 228 cases recorded in 2024, human rights groups and legal advocates caution that the lower figure reflects a growing reluctance by state authorities to properly classify gender-based killings.

video693
description: The US House of Representatives voted in favour of the war powers resolution to force US President Donald Trump to seek Congress approval for military action against Iran, in Washington DC on Wednesday. 
Four Republicans backed the resolution as the House passed it 215 to 208 in favour. 
After the vote, the resolution goes to the Senate, where the measure must be taken up. The conflict, running for more than 90 days, is beyond a threshold that would require the president to seek Congress's approval to continue waging war under the 1973 War Powers Act. The White House rejects this and argues that a ceasefire has been in place since April 8.
The vote's impact is symbolic, however, as a two-thirds majority is needed to override a presidential veto.

The administration insists the restructuring is necessary to tackle crime, control irregular migration, and slim down the state, with a 'National Reconstruction plan' aimed at boosting growth through tax reforms and state modernisation.

I think this is what we can learn from Russia, especially when it comes to the utilisation of digital technology on conducting such kind of large events. This is, I think, one of the most impressive things which I have seen," Jirru said.
The diplomat added that SPIEF was an important platform that brings together many countries to discuss issues relating to the economy, investment, trade and partnership.
Genet Jirru also mentioned that Ethiopian businesses were eager to collaborate with their Russian counterparts.
"It's [a] 128 year old partnership. So, you know, the age itself tells you. But what I can tell you currently, the interaction and the economic relationship between the two countries is on the making," he said. "This kind of platform also gives us an opportunity to interact with various Russian companies. We are meeting at their booths and discussing potential investment opportunities with Ethiopia. Only this year we have a number of Russian companies who have actually started operating and also on feasibility study on further investment in Ethiopia."
The 29th St Petersburg International Economic Forum (SPIEF) takes place on June 3-6. More than 20,000 people are set to attend, with politicians from around 76 countries making the journey. In addition, a US official - Chairman of the US Commission on Fine Arts Rodney Mims Cook Jr - will attend for the first time since 2017.
Since its establishment in 1997, the forum has served as a platform for international dialogue on global economic issues. Vladimir Putin has taken part in the event regularly since 2005.

description: The Inter-American Conference on Social Security in Mexico City welcomed football fans with an exhibition featuring memorabilia from the 1970 and 1986 World Cups in Mexico ahead of the upcoming 2026 tournament. 
Footage shows visitors touring the exhibit, looking at treasured pieces on display, such as photographs, tickets, and jerseys. 
The exhibit also featured 'Pelé's Room', a recreation of the space where the Brazilian star stayed during the 1970 World Cup in Mexico. The space displayed original objects that belonged to the former soccer player, including a Brazil national team jersey and a pair of sandals. 
"We have his signed and certified shirts. Well, I mean, what I could say is that we have a treasure here," Pedro Kumamoto Aguilar, Secretary General of the CISS, remarked. 
He explained that the project to open the room dedicated to Pelé began to take shape four or five years ago. For its development, the institution collaborated with the Brazilian Embassy and various foundations. 
The exhibit, titled Collective Memory 70 and 86: The City That Never Stops Playing, brings together about 600 pieces of memorabilia contributed by city residents from the 1970 and 1986 World Cups.
The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be held from 11 June to 19 July across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. It will be the first World Cup to feature 48 teams, expanding from the previous 32-team format and increasing the number of matches from 64 to 104.

video708
description: Huge waves battered the coast of Nichinan city in Miyazaki Prefecture as Tropical Storm Jangmi moved along Japan’s Pacific coastline on Tuesday. 
Footage shows large swells crashing into the shoreline as winds strengthened ahead of the storm’s passage. 
Authorities warned of further disruption as Jangmi tracked north-east towards the Kanto region, including Tokyo and surrounding prefectures. 
The Japan Meteorological Agency urged residents along the Pacific coast to remain alert for high waves, heavy rain, swollen rivers, flooding and landslides. 
Jangmi had earlier made landfall in Wakayama Prefecture with typhoon-strength winds before weakening to a tropical storm. The system brought sustained winds of around 90 kilometres per hour. It later moved to about 150 kilometres south of Tokyo with sustained winds of 25 metres per second. 
The storm disrupted transport and power supplies across Japan, with hundreds of flights cancelled, train services delayed or suspended, and tens of thousands of households losing electricity. 
Residents in affected coastal areas were advised to follow official warnings and avoid approaching the shoreline as sea conditions worsened.

description: Snowboarders and skiers descended on the stunning, powder-white slopes of the Krasnaya Polyana Resort in Sochi for the famous Bonus Summer Camp festival.
Footage shot on Tuesday shows some performing amazing tricks on their snowboards.
"The mountain valley is naturally shaped like a bowl, so when clouds gather above it, they help to preserve the snow very well for a very long time. That is precisely why we are the first to open the season and the last to close it," said Andrei Kotov, the ski resort’s Product Marketing Head.
According to snowboarder Denis Leontiev, the slope is divided into five areas for different skill levels.
"One is for beginners who are just taking their first steps on snowboards and skis; the second is for those who are a bit more advanced - that’s where kids who already know how to snowboard come to learn tricks. Then we have two jumps that are more suited to teenagers. The fourth area is for jibbing where snowboarders and skiers, no matter their levels, can slide rails and perform various tricks. There’s also a large jump," he explained.
Resort visitor Evgeni Matveev noted the record amount of snow this year: "We’ve never seen anything like it before."
"The atmosphere is amazing - there are so many people here, especially children," the man added.
The Bonus Summer Camp festival runs from June 1-28, offering participants a  30,000-square-metre summer snow park set up 2,050 metres above sea level.

video720
description: Several hotel groups have reduced or suspended operations in Cuba amid the oil blockade and US sanctions. 

Footage filmed in in Havana on Tuesday show several deserted hotels, including an establishment operated by Melia. The chain, the largest foreign operator in Cuba, announced the "immediate cessation" of accommodation services at 15 hotels, citing  "geopolitical, social, legal, and economic" reasons. 

The measure worsens the crisis in the country's tourism sector, which received 328,608 international visitors between January and April, 55.8% fewer than in the same period of the previous year, according to data from the National Office of Statistics and Information (ONEI). 

"During Obama's time, tourism flowed very easily. There were two or three cruise ships in the port, and tourism was everywhere. <…> At the moment, there are neither ships nor planes nor anything. We are totally at zero with tourism," said Pedro Hernandez, a driver who offers tourist rides in a classic car.

Meanwhile, Raidel Cervantes, a restaurant worker, called the situation  'precarious'. "We have the climate, we have the music, we have the joy, we have everything, but if there's no one to offer this to, then what do we do? <…> We are in trouble."

The cessation of operations comes amid pressure from US President Donald Trump on Cuba. On May 20, the U.S. justice system filed charges against former Cuban President Raul Castro and five other people, accusing them of being responsible for the deaths of four individuals, including three U.S. citizens, following the downing of two small planes in 1996. 

In response to these accusations, the Cuban government has maintained that the aircraft entered its airspace illegally and that the actions of the authorities were in accordance with current legality.

This follows decades of tensions between the United States and Cuba, recently marked by tighter sanctions and the blockade promoted by the Trump administration against fuel shipments to the island under threat of sanctions, a measure that caused a deepening energy crisis.

Protesters had gathered against a planned 50-bed Ebola isolation facility at Laikipia Air Base, intended for asymptomatic US citizens exposed to the virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo or Uganda. 
Critics say the centre could put Kenyans at risk and accuse Washington of using an African country as a 'dumping ground'. 
US officials say the facility would monitor exposed people who are not showing symptoms, while symptomatic patients would be treated elsewhere. Kenya has reported no Ebola cases. 
President William Ruto defended the plan, saying it was part of a long-running health partnership with the United States and would strengthen Kenya’s preparedness. 
"I gave the okay because it was an agreement and a partnership with friends who have worked with Kenya for 30 or 40 years. The American government has supported us <...> They have deployed huge resources in Kenya to work with us on HIV/AIDS and other diseases," he said. 
Kenya’s High Court has extended a suspension on the facility for three weeks and ordered the government to disclose agreements linked to the project. The next hearing is scheduled for June 23.

The 32-year-old New Zealand defender has become one of the most talked-about names ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup after an Argentine social media campaign transformed him from a relatively unknown player into an overnight global sensation.

Payne’s social media following exploded from around 4,000 followers to more than 4.7 million within days after Argentine influencer Valen Scarsini, known online as 'El Scarso,' launched a campaign to make the World Cup’s 'least-known player' famous.

"We have to start mentioning Tim Payne everywhere,” Scarsini told his followers. “We have to make videos featuring the legend of Tim Payne. We have to get Tim Payne on everyone's lips."

The campaign quickly spread across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, generating millions of interactions and drawing attention from international media outlets and football fans worldwide.

"To be honest, it was really strange," said sports business agent Juan Jose Romero, who was contacted about potentially managing Payne’s social media accounts. "Within hours, teams and agencies from around the world had already reached him. He already had a PR person and an agent."

description: In Hue, artisan Vo Ngoc Hung, affectionately referred to as the ‘King of Leaves,’ redefines the phrase ‘turn over a new leaf,’ skillfully transforming ordinary forest leaves into durable art pieces that are both usable and wearable, such as fans, umbrellas, handbags, and the iconic conical hats.

Footage captured on Tuesday reveals Vo’s workshop nestled in the historic Kim Long ward of Hue, which serves as both a quaint home studio and a living natural museum. 

Visitors are invited to experience the traditional craft firsthand or engage in interactive leaf-art classes in this intimate, family-operated space.

“The first step is to select and harvest the leaves. After that, I soak them; prior to soaking, I boil them in a baking soda solution to eliminate the odour of decomposing leaves. Once soaked for about one and a half months, I clean the leaves with a brush, ensuring that only the leaf veins remain,” Hung says on the process.

“After brushing, I inspect and remove any remaining stains, then proceed to arrange and shape the conical hat,” he adds.

“I aim to explore new and innovative elements, rather than strictly follow traditional methods, for I realise I can never compare to the essence they’ve held for hundreds of years. To innovate, you must believe in yourself; regardless of success or failure, you alone are responsible,” he shares.

Employing a meticulous technique, Vo processes almond tree leaves, stripping away pulp to create delicate, lace-like skeletons that are layered, sewn, and adorned with iconic scenes.

Under Hung's skilled hands, delicate leaves are ‘reborn’ to carry the distinctive imagery of the Perfume River and Ngu Mountain region.

description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese hosted Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale in Canberra on Tuesday for an official welcome at Parliament House, in Wale’s first overseas visit since taking office last month.

“The Prime Minister's decision to choose Australia for his first overseas visit reflects the closeness of our relationship,” the Australian PM said.

During the press conference, Wale said he would be reviewing a security pact signed with Beijing under the previous administration, which he had previously argued should be made public. 

"I haven't been afforded a copy even of that agreement until a day before I left, so I haven't had a good look at it... I've been praying and fasting about it, but of course, you know, the cabinet will need to have a look at these things," Wale said. 

"There is a non-disclosure clause in it, so I couldn't show it to you right away," he revealed, but confirmed that "we are going to be reviewing, as we are reviewing other security agreements that we have with many other countries."

The security pact, signed in 2022, drew criticism from Australia, New Zealand and the US over the potential for a larger Chinese military presence in the South Pacific, as it was not made public.

When pressed on whether the Solomon Islands would look beyond Beijing for critical infrastructure financing, Wale confirmed a strategic pivot toward other allies. 

"Of course, we've just recently signed the DFC agreement with the US, and so we will be looking to the US as well," Wale stated, adding that he is pushing Washington to fast-track entry into the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) compact to secure alternative "sources of financing that we would be looking for for critical infrastructure."

Beijing remains the primary external creditor to the Solomon Islands, after the Pacific nation's debt to Chinese banks for infrastructure developments doubled over the past year to reach $37 million.

Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning maintained a diplomatic stance on Wednesday, noting that "China and the Solomon Islands are comprehensive strategic partners in the new era, committed to mutual respect and common development." Mao added that Beijing stands ready to work with the Solomon Islands' new government.

To help the archipelago navigate its current financial challenges, Albanese announced that Australia would be providing 200 million Solomon dollars ($24.9 mil) to help cover the cost of recovery from tropical cyclone Maila and address current energy issues.

Footage shows Emmanuel Macron and First Lady Brigitte Macron welcoming Paul Kagame and the First Lady Jeannette Kagame to Elysee Palace before officials enter the building under formal reception protocols.

It comes as France continued efforts to reset relations with Rwanda after years of tension linked to the 1994 genocide and later political disputes.

In recent years, both sides have moved to rebuild ties, focusing on security cooperation in the Great Lakes region.

description: The chairperson of the National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE), Melatework Hailu, described the country’s election as 'successful' despite setbacks linked to security concerns, speaking at a press conference in Addis Ababa on Tuesday. 
"The board deployed a monitoring team to investigate. Some of the suggestions that came were found to be true on the ground, so the board took action," Hailu said, addressing reports of ineligible individuals participating in the vote. 
"Our election officials who have committed misconduct or have been dismissed have a duty that they are expected to fulfil," she continued, adding, "When they are found to have violated that duty, the board will take legal action." 
Hailu went on to say that the NEBE also took firm action to remove administrative personnel and security officers allegedly dressed in civilian clothing from polling stations to ensure a fair process. 
"If we were to list the challenges, they are very many and extensive; but the board has been following this from the bottom up and taking corrective measures," she pointed out. 
"The election, however, was a process that was completed with the intended purpose <...> with over 40 million voters casting their votes. So, taking all of these together, I dare or believe that it was 'successful'," Hailu added. 
The board excluded 46 of 176 constituencies from Monday's vote due to ongoing conflict, including all 38 in Tigray, eight in Amhara, and areas affected by localised disruptions in Oromia. In total, 143 polling stations were unable to operate out of more than 50,000 nationwide, according to media reports. 
More than 50 million people have registered to vote out of a population of around 130 million, with voters electing 500 members of the House of Peoples' Representatives as well as regional and city council representatives, according to the NEBE. 
Under Ethiopia's parliamentary system, the party winning a legislative majority selects the prime minister. 
Incumbent PM Abiy Ahmed has been in power for eight years and leads the Prosperity Party. The party has been governing since 2019, succeeding the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), which was the ruling coalition from 1991 until 2018.

description: FBI Director Kash Patel officially launched Operation Summer Heat 2.0 on Tuesday, a nationwide law enforcement surge designed to target violent crime, street gangs, and drug trafficking across the United States. 

Speaking in West Virginia, Patel announced that the initiative is starting with Operation Turf War, a coordinated crackdown that marks the opening of the federal government's summer security campaign.

“We are going to go to the epicentre of guns and drugs. And what that means is we are going to take out localised street gangs wherever they are,” Patel said during the press conference. 

Lauding the successes of phase one last year, he added, “Operation Summer Heat netted 8,600 arrests, 7,750 search warrants executed, 2,300 firearms taken off the street and 45,000 kilograms of cocaine. That's just a three-month surge from last summer.”

The FBI chief noted that the momentum established by these early enforcement actions will be maintained through a sustained, months-long effort involving thousands of personnel.

“We will go after every animal, every predator, every drug trafficker, every terrorist that dares to come into our country and try to take away our freedoms because they're jealous of the way we live,” he added.

The Trump administration has escalated the war on drugs into a major international offensive, formally classifying fentanyl as a weapon of mass destruction and major cartels as foreign terrorist organisations. 

Operation Turf War, the first phase of Operation Summer Heat 2.0, will now begin a 95-day operational window targeting localised gang epicentres nationwide.

video740
description: Civil Guard officers assisted firefighting operations during a wildfire in Spain's El Valle on Tuesday, as crews worked to contain the blaze and secure surrounding areas.

Footage shows Civil Guard officers supporting emergency teams as smoke rises from the affected hillside.

The fire in the Carrascoy–El Valle area has scorched around 110 hectares of pine forest and shrubland and triggered a large-scale emergency response, with roughly 250 ground personnel and 12 aerial units deployed.

Authorities also carried out precautionary evacuations of around 50 families, affecting more than 100 residents in nearby districts, including Los Garres and San Jose de la Montana.

The fire broke out during a severe orange weather alert for extreme heat, with temperatures in Murcia reaching over 39°C (102°F). Strong winds further complicated early containment efforts.

Officials said the priority was to protect nearby communities and prevent the fire from reaching residential zones. Local services also managed traffic and restricted access to high-risk areas.

Spain's Military Emergencies Unit (UME) reinforced operations overnight, deploying around 170 troops and 50 vehicles to support firefighting efforts.

No official information on the cause of the blaze or final damage assessment has yet been confirmed by authorities.

description: Striking teachers from the National Coordinating Committee of Education Workers (CNTE) blocked major roads and destroyed large football sculptures in Mexico City on Tuesday. The installations, part of the ‘World Cup Giants’ exhibition on Paseo de la Reforma, were targeted during a nationwide strike called just days before the opening of the FIFA 2026 World Cup.

Footage shows union members using ropes to topple one of the giant figures near the Angel of Independence monument, before stripping and setting fire to the clothing and football of another installation. Protesters also defaced the exhibition with graffiti reading 'If there is no solution, the ball will not roll', whilst simultaneous blockades across key junctions caused severe traffic disruption throughout the capital.

Union leaders stated the escalation was a direct response to a violent crackdown on Monday near the Zocalo square, where they claim riot police used tear gas and rubber bullets against marching teachers as they began an indefinite national strike . 

While capital authorities have denied using such munitions, union officials reported several injuries, including one demonstrator who lost an eye.

Octavio Romero, a teacher who required stitches after being struck in the face, said, "Yesterday we reported and denounced the aggression with which this government received us through the police... they aimed their rubber weapons directly at us."

The CNTE has accused President Claudia Sheinbaum’s administration of prioritising the multi-million-pound World Cup tournament over long-standing labour disputes. The union’s demands include a 100 percent salary increase, the repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE Law, and a return to a state-backed pension scheme that completely bypasses private ‘Afore’ retirement funds.

"The people, the workers, and particularly the residents of Mexico City have increasingly become aware of the process of dispossession and exclusion that this World Cup entails... It is a World Cup that seeks to cover up the problems faced by workers in this country," said Citlali de Jesus Ortiz, a teacher representing Section 22.

During her morning press conference, President Sheinbaum pledged to address demands she deemed ‘feasible’, noting that some grievances had already been partially answered by legislative reforms passed under the previous administration.

The destruction of the exhibition comes with only nine days to go before the Azteca Stadium, or Mexico City Stadium, hosts the opening match between Mexico and South Africa on 11 June.

“This regime, as you have rightfully pointed out, even despite sanctions, even despite all the pressure, has found a way to funnel money and resources to these proxy groups. What’s being discussed is what do they get in exchange,” Rubio explained.

“All of that will be condition-based, meaning there’s not going to be some sort of advanced signing bonus or good faith,” he added.

It comes as Washington and Tehran continue indirect contacts.

Rubio also rejected suggestions that the United States was offering financial incentives to secure the waterway’s reopening.

The Strait of Hormuz is a key route for global oil shipments, and recent disruption has sparked supply concerns worldwide.

Washington has accused Iran of threatening commercial shipping, while Tehran says its actions stem from regional security concerns.

Iran says its nuclear programme is for civilian purposes and has criticised what it calls a ‘double standard’, arguing that other countries in the region have nuclear weapons but do not face the same international pressure.

Tensions escalated further overnight, with reports of US Central Command action near the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian strikes on US-linked positions in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Footage and stills released on Tuesday show the detainee in the custody of Army personnel and state agents, wearing a brown shirt, blue trousers, and black trainers.

In an official statement, Mexico's Security Cabinet reported that the capture was executed during a coordinated operation involving the Secretariat of National Defence, the National Guard, and state authorities.

According to the National Detention Registry, Gabriel 'N' was arrested on 1 June at 8:15 pm and has been placed at the disposal of the Attorney General's Office (FGR), which will determine his legal status.

The detainee is currently under investigation for his suspected involvement in crimes including kidnapping, extortion, homicide, and drug-related offences. Additionally, he is accused of being linked to the murder of 10 miners in the municipality of La Concordia in January this year.

The arrest comes amidst persistent violence in the state, where rival factions of the Sinaloa Cartel have been locked in a bloody dispute for control of the organisation since 2024, following the capture of the criminal group's co-founder, Ismael 'El Mayo' Zambada, in the United States.

description: An aid worker described the situation at Ebola epicentre in Ituri province's Mongbwalu, as authorities and international organisations stepped up containment efforts. 
“Cars were stoned because the community was angry that a member of their community had died,”  Professor Yap Boum, Incident Manager at Africa CDC, said in Bunia on Tuesday. 
It comes after a joint mission involving the World Health Organisation (WHO), the World Food Programme (WFP), Africa CDC visited the epicentre. 
Boum said Mongbwalu has recorded 43 confirmed cases, with more than 100 deaths since the start of the outbreak, calling it 'a critical epidemiological situation.' 
Footage shows passengers undergoing disinfection at health control points and medical staff enforcing screening procedures as part of ongoing outbreak control measures. 
“We have committed to rapidly deploying community liaisons and community leaders so that the community is part of this response,” he said. 
He added that a laboratory would be installed in Mongbwalu in coordination with WHO and the government to enable faster testing, while treatment facilities would be expanded. 
An Ebola outbreak was declared by the DRC and Uganda on May 15, after laboratory tests confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease. WHO named it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. 
According to local authorities, there are 125 confirmed cases and 17 confirmed deaths in the DRC, alongside nine cases and one death in neighbouring Uganda. The DRC has also over 1,000 suspected cases and at least 246 suspected deaths.

video755
description: Shop owners in Dhaka have urged the government to extend newly reinstated market closing times beyond 7 PM, when most customers prefer to shop during the cooler evening hours. 
Footage filmed on Tuesday shows the closed entrances of the China Town Shopping Centre, while traders and security personnel at Baitul Mukarram Market shut down stores in compliance with the new regulations. 
“Customers come more in the evening, very few during the day,” said shop owner Mohammad Naeem. “Our markets are crowded after Maghrib prayers. Since it is hot during the day, customers come when the weather is cooler. It would be good for us if the market stayed open until 10 p.m.” 
Traders warned that the measure could have wider economic consequences in a city heavily dependent on evening commerce. 
“If the market closes at 7 PM, it will definitely have a huge impact on the economy,” said Nazrul Islam. “Dhaka city is known as a commercial hub. Most sales happen in the evening. If the government allows markets to open later and close at 9 or 10 PM, it would be better for everyone.” 
Others said shoppers often do not have enough time to visit markets before the mandatory closure. “They would feel more comfortable coming to the market and shopping if stores remained open until 9 or 10 PM,”  said Abul Hossain. 
The Bangladeshi government officially reinstated a nationwide 7 PM closing time for shopping malls, markets and retail shops on June 1, reversing a temporary extension granted during the Eid al-Adha period when businesses were allowed to operate until 10 PM. 
The order, issued by the Power Division, is part of efforts to conserve electricity and manage the national grid amid rising summer temperatures and increasing energy costs. Authorities have also ordered all billboard and promotional lighting to be switched off and required fairs, exhibitions and cultural events to end by 7 PM. 
Essential services, including pharmacies, hospitals, hotels, restaurants and fresh food markets, remain exempt from the restrictions. 
The measures come as Bangladesh faces mounting energy pressures. The country imports around 95 percent of its oil, primarily from Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and faces heightened risk as supply routes remain unstable. 
Shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for roughly 20 percent of global oil and liquefied natural gas, have driven prices higher and strained imports. The disruption follows escalating tensions after the United States and Israel launched joint military operations against Iran on February 28.

description: Dr Mehmet Oz - TV star turned Administrator of the Centres for Medicare and Medicaid Services in the Trump administration - was asked about the row over an Ebola treatment centre for US citizens in Kenya, as he took a media briefing in DC on Tuesday.

"On Ebola, if Kenya does end up blocking the US quarantine facility there, and it seems like they might since the Kenyan courts are delaying it, where will Americans who have been exposed end up going?" he was asked. "And then why can't they just come to the United States?"

Kenya has seen fierce protests over the plans, with critics there accusing the US of treating Africans as 'second class citizens', using the country as a 'dumping ground', and putting lives at risk - especially given that Kenya does not have an Ebola outbreak itself like the DRC.

Oz hit back, saying it was about having a facility in relatively close proximity: "the main issue with having a facility close to the Democratic Republic of the Congo is if a patient is sick, again, I'll speak as a heart doctor, I want to take the patient to the OR that's right next door to the room they're sick in, not to the building next to them or to three buildings two blocks away because that time is precious to us."

"You have a golden hour in many of these instances around trauma, but for illnesses, it's also relatively short," he went on. "So we are confident, and the State Department's working on this diligently, that they're going to be able to work out something with Kenya. There has already been a fair amount of communication around this issue."

There are plans for a 50-bed isolation unit at Laikipia Air Base, near Nanyuki, for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo or Uganda. The site is intended for asymptomatic US citizens, including health workers, diplomats and military personnel. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said Washington “cannot and will not allow any cases of Ebola to enter the United States,” fuelling accusations that the US is shifting risk onto Kenya instead of bringing exposed citizens home. 

The Law Society of Kenya and the Katiba Institute have challenged the plan in the Kenyan courts, arguing that the government is acting without proper public participation, transparency or adequate safeguards. Kenya’s High Court has extended a halt on the facility for three weeks and ordered the government to disclose agreements, protocols and hazard assessments within seven days. The next hearing is set for June 23.

President William Ruto defended the plan, saying it was part of a long-running health partnership with the United States and would strengthen Kenya’s preparedness. "I gave the okay because it was an agreement and a partnership with friends who have worked with Kenya for 30 or 40 years. The American government has supported us <...> They have deployed huge resources in Kenya to work with us on HIV/AIDS and other diseases," he said. 

US officials say the facility would only monitor people exposed to Ebola who are not showing symptoms, while symptomatic patients would be treated elsewhere.

description: Designer Ariel Cuadra and human rights organisation H.I.J.O.S. Capital launched a sticker album dedicated to the Mothers and Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo, commemorating the 50th anniversary of the 1976 coup that ushered in the last civic-military dictatorship in Argentina (1976-1983).
Footage captured in Buenos Aires on Tuesday shows the project's creators showcasing the album's stickers. The initiative aims to promote memory, truth, and justice through a popular format that transcends generations and emulates the traditional Panini World Cup sticker album. 
Ahead of the 2026 World Cup, Cuadra expressed how the unique album drew inspiration from the classic football stickerbook and was a way of paying tribute to mothers and grandmothers searching for their disappeared loved ones.
"I tried to transform this from the image of a football idol to our icons of democracy. I call them our figures of democracy because they are international role models for human rights, for the human rights struggle in our country. And I think that paying tribute to them through this piece, however small it may be, has generated a great deal of buzz,” he said. 
Giselle Tepper, a member of H.I.J.O.S. Capital, explained that each figurine includes biographical information about different Mothers and Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo, such as their date of birth, whether they are still alive and active in the search for justice, or whether they have passed away. It also includes information about their disappeared sons and daughters. 
"We think it's very important to be able to continue talking about this because for the sons, daughters, and human rights organisations, the mothers and grandmothers are the example that started this whole journey and, of course, continues it today. So I think it's also a way of embracing them and saying that yes, they are our Messis, our Maradonas of memory," said Tepper.
The album is available free of charge in PDF format through the official H.I.J.O.S. Capital website and, according to the organisation, has already proved highly successful, attracting a large number of downloads. 
The Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo Civil Association aims to locate and return to their families the babies and children appropriated during the last Argentine military dictatorship. The Mothers of Plaza de Mayo, for their part, emerged to demand the reappearance of their children who were detained and disappeared during that period.

description: Renovation work continues on the Mexico City Metro just nine days before the World Cup, with doubts raised over whether it will be completed in time.

The works in question are being performed on line 2, which connects to the historical centre of the capital and will serve as one of the key routes for tourists during the tournament. 

In footage captured during a tour conducted on Sunday, workers were observed performing maintenance tasks, with stairways seen without tiles and construction materials scattered around. 

At Bellas Artes station, the walls can be seen covered with reddish marble finishes, as well as new decorative lamps and motorised walkways and the conventional turnstiles replaced. At Hidalgo station, construction signage was prominent, along with a new chandelier. 

Some metro users said they believe that the station works will not be complete in time for the World Cup, despite the head of government Clara Brugada stating that they will be ready between June 7 and 8. 

"They will probably bring in a lot more labour, a lot more workers to finish as soon as possible, but I think they won't finish the renovations," said user Luis Arias. "I see the whole station and it's not even functional yet (...) there's no way it will be ready, and I think Mexico will have a worse role with this. I mean, seeing that everything is incomplete, third-worldism at its peak," added student Ana Sofia. 

Users also complain that the focus on aesthetic changes rather than improvements to the metro's functionality issues. 

"I think the renovations are for foreign benefit, because they are very aesthetic, very superficial to a certain extent. There are many infrastructure problems (...) So, really everything they are doing has no benefit for daily users," another opined.

description: Activists marched on Kenya’s Ministry of Health in Nairobi on Tuesday - carrying a coffin - and got themselves arrested, as they protested against a proposed US-backed Ebola quarantine facility.
Critics say the centre for US citizens exposed to the virus puts Kenyans at risk - and is using an African country as a 'dumping ground'. Footage shows protesters in biohazard suits clashing with police as they tried to enter the ministry while carrying a mock coffin for President William Ruto - and getting detained.
“What we are saying is very simple. We are going to resist every step and mechanism by William Ruto to establish a quarantine centre in Kenya,” one protester said outside the gates. 
The anger centres on a planned 50-bed isolation unit at Laikipia Air Base, near Nanyuki, for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo or Uganda. The site is intended for asymptomatic US citizens, including health workers, diplomats and military personnel. 
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said Washington “cannot and will not allow any cases of Ebola to enter the United States,” fuelling accusations that the US is shifting risk onto Kenya instead of bringing exposed citizens home. 
"It is not lost to us that this government signed an agreement with the US government that gave up our bio data and patient medical records to the US for a period of more than five years. This is in contravention to public safety and national interests," one activist said. 
"Importing Ebola into Kenya would be giving us a challenge too big to surmount. We have given the Ministry of Health 72 hours, a 72-hour ultimatum to respond to our concerns and demands. Failure to do so will compel us to pursue action and peaceful public assemblies," he added. 
The Law Society of Kenya and the Katiba Institute have challenged the plan in court, arguing that the government acted without proper public participation, transparency or adequate safeguards. 
Kenya’s High Court has extended a block on the facility for three weeks and ordered the government to disclose agreements, protocols and hazard assessments within seven days. The next hearing is set for June 23. 
The protests have already turned deadly. Two people were reportedly killed during demonstrations in Nanyuki on Monday. 
President William Ruto defended the plan, saying it was part of a long-running health partnership with the United States and would strengthen Kenya’s preparedness. 
"I gave the okay because it was an agreement and a partnership with friends who have worked with Kenya for 30 or 40 years. The American government has supported us <...> They have deployed huge resources in Kenya to work with us on HIV/AIDS and other diseases," he said. 
US officials say the facility would only monitor people exposed to Ebola who are not showing symptoms, while symptomatic patients would be treated elsewhere. Critics argue Kenya’s health system should not be asked to carry the risk of a facility designed primarily for US nationals.

"The Marine Corps sees urgent needs for patrol along beaches and coastlines, and the Coast Guard has similar needs for patrols around Pratas Island and the Spratly Islands. The Army also has specific requirements for base perimeter patrol," he stressed.

description: Niger farmers are finding innovative ways to recycle the massive amount of organic waste generated during Eid al-Adha. Instead of letting the remains of the holiday's sacrificial animals clog up city streets, agriculturalists are converting the waste into premium, low-cost fertiliser to boost local food security.

Footage from Zinder on Sunday shows farmers collecting discarded animal waste, piling it in bags, and burning the carcasses in the open to make organic fertiliser.

"It all started with a simple observation. Several years ago, I noticed that whenever an animal carcass was discarded in my field, the area became more fertile after it decomposed. I concluded that if I used organic animal waste generated during Tabaski (Eid), it could produce the same result," said local farmer Laouli Roufai.

Roufai has been producing fertiliser for the last three years, and stresses that the product also serves as a protection mechanism against wandering animals invading fields due to the dislike of hides and stomach contents.

"I no longer need to cut down trees to build a fence. The only problem is that I can obtain only a limited quantity. I cannot ask the entire neighbourhood to collect waste for me. I make do with whatever I can find in my area," the farmer added.

President of Young Environmental Volunteers Mohamed Amadou Barhalle thinks that the initiatives should be encouraged. 

"Instead of throwing this waste away, people can dig a pit on their property and gather it there. After six to eight weeks, it turns into natural compost that can be used in agricultural fields," Barhalle added.

According to statistics from the Sahel nation, the capital city of Niamey alone sees approximately 400,000 sheep sacrificed annually, with large amounts of animal waste often disposed of improperly, contributing to sanitation challenges and environmental pollution.

"Every day when I go out on the water, when I’m gliding above the waves and all I can hear is the wind - that’s something I couldn’t live without," he said.

description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed cast his ballot in Jimma Zone, Oromia Region, on Monday, warning of alleged interference in the national election by external forces. 
Footage shows the prime minister arriving at a polling station, completing registration, entering the voting booth, and casting his ballot. 
"In order to prevent the election from going smoothly as planned, Ethiopia's historical enemies have deployed their forces; they have carried out propaganda; they have tried to make us believe that democratic elections are not possible in Ethiopia," Ahmed told reporters after the vote. 
"However, the Ethiopian people [...] have shown the great spirit of heroism and have been holding the election in all the streets I have come to since morning," he continued. "They do not need a mentor or a guide to build their state [...] and to decide what they want to build in Ethiopia." 
The remarks follow the National Election Board of Ethiopia's (NEBE) decision to exclude 46 of 176 constituencies from Monday's vote due to ongoing conflict, including all 38 in Tigray, eight in Amhara, and localised disruptions in Oromia. In total, 143 stations were unable to operate out of over 50,000 locations across the country, according to media reports. 
Ahmed also referenced past elections in the Horn of Africa, noting a possible re-vote for those unable to participate. 
"The people will express their needs; if it's convenient for them tomorrow, then all these voters got up in the morning and lined up for a fee," he explained. 
According to the NEBE, more than 50 million people have registered to vote out of a population of around 130 million, with voters electing 500 members of the House of Peoples' Representatives as well as regional and city council representatives. 
Under Ethiopia's parliamentary system, the party winning a legislative majority selects the prime minister. 
Ahmed, in power for eight years, leads the Prosperity Party, which has governed since 2019 after succeeding the Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), the ruling coalition from 1991 to 2018.

description: Burundi’s coastline is facing widespread destruction as Lake Tanganyika expands beyond its shores, submerging homes, critical infrastructure, and farmland. The ongoing crisis has left local businesses and landowners facing financial ruin as they struggle to survive.

Footage filmed in Bujumbara on Friday captures the devastating, ongoing impact of the rising waters, showing completely abandoned and partially submerged lakeside businesses that were once the hub of local tourism.

"These floods have set back the development of the beaches. Everyone suffered significant losses. Some are still in shock and will never recover," said Omar Manirambona, owner of Safi Beach, who has seen the entire business he invested in since 2017 gradually engulfed by the rising lake.

The economic fallout extends far beyond the tourism sector. In rural communities south of Bujumbura, rising waters have swallowed vital agricultural land, decimating the primary source of income for local families.

"We lost our land, our oil palms, and our cassava fields. As you can see, there is nothing left but flooded land," explained farmer Violette Niyokwizera, a resident of Migera.

Environmental experts point directly to climate change and regional weather patterns as the primary drivers of the environmental disaster.

"The rising waters of Lake Tanganyika are caused by excessive rainfall hitting not only Burundi, but the entire sub-region - including northeastern Congo and western Rwanda, flowing down from Lake Kivu through the Rusizi River," said Jean Marie Sabushimike, a professor at the University of Burundi specialising in climate change and disaster management.

The massive lake, shared between Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, and Zambia, has failed to return to normal levels, defying expectations that the water would recede following historic floods triggered by the severe El Nino weather phenomenon.

description: Thousands of Tenggerese Hindus embarked on a treacherous pilgrimage to the jagged rim of Mount Bromo, a 2,329-metre-tall active volcano in East Java, to participate in the annual Yadnya Kasada ceremony on Monday.

Footage shows devotees ascending the narrow paths leading to the crater, laden with traditional offerings, including colourful fruits, vegetables, cash, and even livestock as dawn breaks. 

Praying to the mountain gods, they hurled these items into the abyss below, where daring villagers balanced on the ash-slick slopes, equipped with wide butterfly nets and sarongs, ready to catch the falling sacrifices, believing that catching these offerings mid-air brings divine luck.

Bambang Suprapto, Chair of the Kasada Ceremony Organising Committee, noted before the ascent, “Later, we will climb up to the crater of Mount Bromo to offer our harvest. From morning until afternoon, and in the evening, we will conclude with the Kasada rain to mark the end of the activities.”

Devotee Vivin Irawati added, “It's an offering to the earth, consisting of crops, green onions, and livestock.”

This tradition, deeply rooted in local mythology and passed down through generations, serves as an expression of gratitude to Sang Hyang Widhi, the all-powerful God in Balinese Hinduism, for the blessings of life, prosperity, and agricultural abundance over the past year.

This ritual is not only a religious event but also one of Indonesia's most distinctive cultural attractions, drawing thousands of visitors each year.

Through the Yadnya Kasada ritual, the Tengger community prays for continued blessings, safety, fertile land, and generous harvests, all while preserving their rich traditions amidst the challenges of modernisation.

description: Shiva, a seven-month-old female jaguar injured by more than 90 lead pellets, has finally been transferred to La Paz for veterinary treatment after weeks of delays caused by roadblocks and fuel shortages in Bolivia.

The cub was taken to the capital in the early hours of Monday in an operation coordinated by the La Paz regional government, through the Departmental Secretariat for the Protection of Mother Earth and Environmental Management, and the Senda Verde wildlife refuge.

Once in La Paz, Shiva was admitted to Semevet Veterinary Hospital, where she underwent CT scans, X-rays, ultrasounds and blood tests before emergency surgery.

Veterinarian and Semevet General Manager Sergio Cuenca Toledo said the tests showed injuries that required immediate intervention, adding that the delay in treatment worsened her condition.

"Further tests have been carried out to determine the amount of lead in her blood. These tests led us to a surgical procedure involving a multidisciplinary team of approximately 12 professionals," he said.

"Unfortunately, the roadblocks have greatly complicated her health," Cuenca added.

The Senda Verde refuge spent weeks warning about the difficulties of transporting animals, securing fuel and obtaining food supplies amid the blockades.

Virginia Ossio, the refuge's co-founder, said Shiva's transfer was only possible thanks to help from private donors.

"We brought her in for her check-up today, two weeks later than planned. We had not been able to leave because of the roadblocks and the lack of petrol. Thanks to the support of many friends who donated to us, we were finally able to gather enough petrol to make the journey," she explained. 

Although the surgery was successful and specialists say Shiva's recovery is promising, her injuries mean she will never be able to return to the wild.

The jaguar was rescued on March 14 near Viru Viru, in Santa Cruz, after a family reported finding a badly injured cub. Later examinations found more than 90 pellets lodged in different parts of her body, as well as fractures and severe infections.

The case comes as roadblocks continue to disrupt several regions of Bolivia. The protests, led by trade unions and social organisations, have been ongoing for more than three weeks and are mainly demanding the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz.

The blockades caused major problems for transport, supplies and mobility across parts of the country.

description: Thousands of members of the National Coordinator of Education Workers (CNTE) launched an indefinite national strike on Monday, demanding a pension overhaul, better working conditions, and a 100 percent salary increase, triggering violent clashes with riot police in Mexico City as the country prepares for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Footage shows the march escalating along Paseo de la Reforma towards the Zocalo, where heavy metal barricades and a massive security deployment blocked access to the Plaza de la Constitucion ahead of World Cup promotional events. 

Tension boiled over when several protesters attempted to breach the perimeter using pipes and wooden sticks. Capital police responded with tear gas to disperse the crowd, injuring at least two teachers.

"They greet us with repression," said Octavio Romero, an injured educator from the CNTE’s Section XIV, who alleged that officers deliberately targeted protesters. "I want to be direct. It wasn't a stray rubber bullet; it was direct aggression from those police officers. We hold the federal government responsible."

The clash highlights the growing friction between Mexico's domestic social crises and its international obligations as a World Cup co-host. Protesters expressed deep resentment over the state funds and security resources poured into football infrastructure while public education remains underfunded.

"The federal government only cares about a ball rolling," said Dina Corona, a teacher from Section XXII, pointing to the nearby World Cup preparations. "We are the focus of the world right now, and we cannot just pretend that nothing is happening in a World Cup venue. Of course not!"

At the heart of the dispute is a demand for the total repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE Law, a controversial piece of legislation that dismantled the traditional state pension scheme, raising the retirement age and shifting public workers toward individual accounts. 

The union wants a return to a system purely defined by years of service and final salary, alongside the reversal of market-driven educational reforms passed under previous administrations.

Prevented from establishing their planned camp in the Zocalo due to the security lockdown, union contingents instead set up an indefinite sit-in across major arteries surrounding the Historic Centre, threatening prolonged disruption to the capital's transport network. 

In response, the Ministry of Public Education issued a statement urging the union to maintain peaceful mobilisations, inviting leaders to resolve the deadlock through formal dialogue alongside the Ministry of the Interior.

Since taking office, Kast has blamed the previous administration of Gabriel Boric for many of the challenges his government faces. Kast promised to restore hope to the voters who elected him, while pushing an agenda focused on public order, security and fiscal restraint.

His administration is seeking to tackle crime, control irregular migration and reduce the size of the state through budget cuts and restructuring. It has also proposed a 'National Reconstruction' plan, including tax reforms, modernisation of state management and measures aimed at boosting growth and employment.

The measures sparked political and social debate, with critics warning they could hit social programmes, education and healthcare.

“Israeli warnings of imminent strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs are deeply concerning and have heightened fear and uncertainty among the population in Lebanon,” he said during a press briefing. 
“We reiterate that civilians and civilian infrastructure must not be targeted. We urge all actors to respect the cessation of hostilities and avoid further escalation,” he added, stressing a diplomatic solution to ‘break the cycle of violence’ on both sides of the borders. 
He added that UN Special Coordinator for Lebanon Jeanine Hennis-Plasschaert continues to engage all sides to honour the agreed ceasefire and push forward with confidence-building measures. 
Dujarric also confirmed that the UN Security Council would convene an emergency session at the request of France to address the rapidly deteriorating situation in Lebanon. 
On the ground, he said UNIFIL peacekeepers have recorded a sharp rise in hostilities, including hundreds of trajectories exchanged across southern Lebanon. 
“Yesterday, they recorded 744 trajectories, including 683 attributed to the IDF,” he said. “On Monday, 400 trajectories were detected, 380 attributed to the IDF, and 22 non-state actors, as well as 12 airstrikes and 59 airspace violations of Lebanese airspace,” adding that further exchanges continued into Monday with additional airstrikes and airspace violations. 
Dujarric refused to be drawn by a question on whether "the Lebanese people have the right to resist those invaders and occupiers," while underlining that the Lebanese armed forces must maintain a strict ‘monopoly of arms’ to protect the nation's borders. 
This comes as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced on Monday that he had ordered continued strikes on Hezbollah 'terror targets' in Beirut, as Israeli forces continue to advance deeper into Lebanese territory. 
Dujarric also fielded a question on whether the UN had a message on whether "the latest escalation in military action between Iran and the United States threatening the ceasefire and talks." 
“The message is one of restraint; the message is to calling on both the Islamic Republic of Iran and the United States to redouble their efforts at diplomacy,” he replied.

"They're not heading in the right direction and it is yet another reason to redouble diplomatic efforts,” he noted. "It's parents' day, right? So what's that song about the thigh bone being connected to the leg bone? Everything is interconnected.” 
President Donald Trump announced a 10-day ceasefire between both sides on April 15, extending it by three weeks on April 23 following direct talks between Lebanese and Israeli officials in Washington. The United States later announced a further 45-day extension in mid-May. 
Meanwhile, the Israeli military has established a 'Yellow Line' in southern Lebanon to prevent residents from returning to areas under its control. The measure echoes a tactic previously used in the Gaza Strip, where civilians are barred from entering designated zones under ceasefire agreements.

description: Hundreds of protesters rallied in the Kenyan town of Nanyuki on Monday to oppose plans to establish an Ebola quarantine facility for American citizens exposed to the virus. 
Footage shows demonstrators marching through the streets, waving Kenyan flags and chanting slogans. Security forces were deployed to oversee the protest, as scenes showed burning barricades before firefighters moved in to extinguish the blazes. 
"We are protesting for the dignity of Nanyuki town, we are protesting to restore order in Nanyuki town, and we are here, every one of us today, to protest against the Ebola quarantine that has been imposed by the American government and Kenyan government," said protester Patrick Wahome. 
"We are asking the American government, we as the people of Kenya, any agreement that you enter with President William Ruto, that agreement is null and void, and we don't want to be part of it," another protester, Charles Iganji, added. 
US officials said that the United States was planning to send Americans exposed to Ebola abroad to a new facility in Kenya instead of flying them back to the United States, at the Laikipia Air Base according to media reports. 
The protests come three days after Kenya's High Court suspended the facility's establishment and barred the arrival of any foreign patients pending the hearing of a petition filed by the Law Society of Kenya and a constitutional watchdog group. 
An Ebola outbreak was declared by the DRC and Uganda on May 15, after laboratory tests confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease. WHO named it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. 
According to local authorities, there are 125 confirmed cases and 17 confirmed deaths in the DRC, alongside nine cases and one death in neighbouring Uganda. The DRC has also over 1,000 suspected cases and at least 246 suspected deaths.
