description: Chinese military expert Senior Colonel Zhou Bo on Saturday argued that Washington's persistent pressure on its partners to shoulder more regional defence costs exposes a fundamental contradiction, noting that such an alliance system cannot function properly if the "big brother" refuses to carry the primary financial weight.

Footage shows officials and delegates arriving at the IISS Shangri-La Dialogue 2026 - Asia’s premier security summit. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Japanese Minister of Defence Shinjiro Koizumi and Chief of Staff of the Indonesian Army Maruli Simanjuntak could also be seen arriving.

“At this summit, the Americans didn't overly hype their own power. Instead, what they repeatedly emphasised is that everyone needs to shoulder and share the burden. Essentially, no one can take advantage of the US moving forward,” Zhou, a fellow at the Centre for International Security and Strategy, said on the sidelines of the event.

Zhou’s comments follow a speech made by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, who used the dialogue to note a shift away from reliance on US military dominance, demanding Indo-Pacific allies significantly increase their defence spending and assume greater operational responsibilities.

“Because you are the 'big brother’ - and the big brother is supposed to contribute the most financially. If your little brothers all have to share the burden equally, then there is an inherent problem with your alliance,” Zhou added.

While Washington frames this burden-sharing as essential for regional stability, Beijing views the strategy as a flawed attempt to outsource the costs of US geopolitical containment efforts, creating concern among smaller regional partners who fear being drawn into a US-China conflict.

Running from May 29-31, this year’s IISS Shangri-La Dialogue arrives at a critical geopolitical juncture, bringing together government figures, military chiefs and security experts to discuss a range of security issues in the Indo-Pacific.

description: Taiwan's legislature approved a 2026 special defence procurement budget of more than 8.81 billion new Taiwan dollars (about 280 million USD) to purchase US weaponry two days before the payment deadline on Friday in Taipei.

"The 2026 Central Government Special Budget for Safeguarding National Security and Strengthening Asymmetric Combat Capabilities Procurement Plan is passed with amendments as per the review report," President of the Legislative Yuan Han Kuo-yu declared. 

The budget saw a reduction of only two million new Taiwan dollars (63,640 USD) in operating expenses compared to the original Cabinet proposal.

Legislative Yuan member Chen Kuan-ting criticised the budget trimming, calling on the legislators to unite in supporting 'national defence capability'.

"Today's result does not mean everything went smoothly," he stated. "Items including commissioned production and commercial procurement - particularly drones, counter-drone systems, and ammunition readiness measures that would complete the military's combat capability and strengthen domestic industries - were unable to pass this time."

The approved budget reportedly allocates 3.92 billion new Taiwan dollars (125 million USD) for M109A7 self-propelled howitzers, 2.79 billion (89 million USD) for HIMARS rocket systems, 1.79 billion (57 million USD) for anti-armour drone missiles, 162 million (five million USD) for Javelin anti-tank missiles and 130 million (four million USD) for TOW 2B anti-tank missiles.

The approval of the budget comes two days before the US deadline for an 800 million new Taiwan dollars (25 million USD) payment on HIMARS systems set for Sunday. Taipei risked jeopardising the procurement programme if the deadline were missed.

The weaponry purchase deal between Taiwan and the US comes amid growing geopolitical friction in the region.

Chinese President Xi Jinping recently issued a direct warning to US President Donald Trump, explicitly stating that the Taiwan question carries a severe risk of direct conflict between the United States and China if not managed with 'extreme care'.

"It is an additional threat for us because drones are carrying explosives," Kaunas said. "Even in Romania, a few days ago, we saw that a drone crashed into a civilian building. This is a new phase of war."

He also warned that balloons currently being used for 'smuggling,' could be adapted to carry explosives or drones.

"Is it a threat? Yes, it is, because you can attach anything you want. You can attach explosives, you can attach drones," he added. 

Kaunas added that Ukraine had also begun using similar balloons to send weapons and drones over distances of more than 1,000 kilometres.

Following the incident in Romania, Western leaders were quick to blame Russia. NATO chief Mark Rutte hit out at Moscow's 'recklessness' while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Russia had 'crossed yet another line'. 

However, speaking with reporters later, Dan revealed that when drones had "passed over the territory of Ukraine, some of them were shot down, and one of them was probably hit over the city of Reni. His (the drone's) trajectory changed, and he hit Galati." 

Asked what might've changed the trajectory, he replied the drone was 'hit kinetically" and was 'shot down'. 

Earlier, the Romanian Defence Ministry also gave a press briefing and insisted that the drone incident was 'not an attack' on the country: "We are dealing with the effects of a conflict taking place in the immediate vicinity of our border. Unfortunately, with direct consequences on the population in the area," said Brigadier General Gheorghe Maxim, Deputy Commander of Romanian Armed Forces Joint Command. 

Vladimir Putin, speaking at the Eurasian Economic Union Forum in Astana, said: "No one can determine the origin of any aircraft until an investigation has been conducted."

An Ebola outbreak was declared by the DRC and Uganda on May 15 after laboratory tests confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease. WHO named it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. 

As of May 21, the WHO said the DRC had reported 83 confirmed cases, including nine deaths, as well as 746 suspected cases and 176 suspected deaths. Later reporting put the toll at more than 900 suspected cases and around 220 suspected deaths. 

Uganda has temporarily closed its borders with the DRC, except for Ebola response teams, humanitarian operations, cargo, food transportation, and security personnel, all of which are subject to strict screening procedures.

description: Around half of the beaches monitored by the Quintana Roo government are under red alert because of high levels of sargassum along the coast.

Footage filmed on Friday at Punta Esmeralda Beach in Playa del Carmen shows workers from the Federal Maritime-Terrestrial Zone and Mexico's Navy removing sargassum using machinery and manual tools.

Zofemat worker Reyna Lopez said the amount of sargassum this year has been heavier than in 2025, with a sharp increase recorded during May.

A local expressed concern that the seaweed could affect tourism, warning that visitors may choose other Mexican destinations with cleaner beaches.

"They said this was going to improve because of the World Cup. But what happens if tourists are in Guadalajara or other places and they see Playa del Carmen covered in sargassum? Other beaches, like Mazatlan in Sinaloa, are clean. Obviously, they may not come here," she explained. 

Sara, a tourist from Germany, said she was surprised by the amount of seaweed on the beach and by the smell, although she said she still planned to enjoy her stay.

"We continue to enjoy here at Punta Esmeralda beach. And we might adapt our plans a bit and maybe go to some islands or more inland, like the inner parts of the peninsula. Yes, we're trying to make the best of it. We continue to enjoy the atmosphere and the good food and the good weather," she said. 

In response to the surge, Mexico's Navy announced in early May that it deployed 150 personnel to reinforce containment and clean-up operations before the sargassum reached the Quintana Roo shoreline.

The Navy also added a new collection vessel capable of gathering up to 600 tonnes of seaweed per day in open water.

description: Farmers in the Nuble region of south-central Chile shared their concern following the decision by the National Sugar Industry (Iansa) not to purchase sugar beets for the 2026-2027 season, a move that threatens to end decades of sugar production in the region.
 
Footage captured on Thursday in Chillan show tractors traversing extensive sugar beet plantations, while farmers inspect the final harvests before the definitive contract closure scheduled for August. 

"This sugar beet we're seeing here will be harvested in 10 or 15 days, and the plant closes on August 15th, and there are no more contracts," explained Marcelo San Martín, President of the Nuble Sugar Beet Growers Association. 

He explained that Iansa was founded and managed by Chileans, but currently operates with the support of a North American investment fund. "That investment fund said: this part of your business isn't profitable, so it's closing, overnight. They couldn't give advance notice because the company is publicly traded," he stated. 

According to farmer Abel Moncada, this measure puts local producers in a difficult situation due to the economic consequences throughout the regional sugar beet production chain. 

"What are we going to plant on those hectares we had earmarked for sugar beets? It affects us farmers, it affects our workers, it affects the businesses around the beet fields, the truckers. It affects us all," he asserted. 

He also criticised the competition from imported sugar and the lack of protective measures for the agricultural sector. "Today, with zero tariffs, they're flooding us with imported sugar, and the government doesn't care that our farmers are disappearing one by one." 

"We're all going to end up in dire straits," he warned, noting that domestic consumers would also suffer. 

Iansa announced the decision in a statement to the Financial Market Commission (CMF), indicating that it is producing sugar at its San Carlos plant in the Nuble region using imported raw sugar instead of beets grown in Chile. 

According to the company, this measure is a response to the drop in international sugar prices and the increase in production costs. While Iansa maintained approximately 440 contracts with farmers in central and southern Chile in 2025, the decision not to renew contracts for the next season leaves domestic producers in limbo. 

Sugar beets have been one of the main crops in Nuble for decades and a major source of rural employment in the area. Farmers warn that the closure of the production cycle not only threatens producers, but also families that depend on agricultural activity, including trade and transport.

video974
description: A team of Argentine and Japanese researchers discovered fossilised remains of a new species of carnivorous dinosaur that inhabited southern Patagonia some 70 million years ago, shortly before the mass extinction of the dinosaurs. The dinosaur has been named 'Kank Australis'. 
Footage recorded in Santa Cruz, where the discovery was made, shows the recovered remains which are being analysed by paleontologist Matias Motta of the Bernardino Rivadavia Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences. Motta indicated that the discovery was made in the town of El Calafate. 
"This dinosaur is unique. It belongs to the Unenlagid group, a group of raptor dinosaurs. Perhaps the most well-known members of this group are the velociraptors from the Northern Hemisphere," he explained. 
The dinosaur measured around two meters long and possessed the typical curved and sharp 'raptor claw' on one of its feet, which it used for hunting. However, the researcher pointed out that it likely had piscivorous habits, meaning it fed primarily on fish, as a result of its teeth. 
"In this case, this dinosaur had conical teeth with ridges that we believe would have served precisely to allow it to fish, preventing fish from escaping when it caught them in the water," he added. 
A study of the neck vertebrae also allowed researchers to infer that the animal had great cervical mobility, comparable to that of modern waterfowl, such as storks, which facilitated its hunting in the water. 
"It reminds us a lot of the fishing habits of storks or herons. So we're talking about a dinosaur that would have lived in aquatic environments, such as lagoons or rivers, a landscape very different from that of present-day Patagonia," Motta noted. According to the paleontologist, this discovery has revealed not only the characteristics of Kank Australis, but has also provided insight into its life just before the extinction of the dinosaurs in Patagonia. 
In addition to the Bernardino Rivadavia Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences, specialists from the Félix de Azara Foundation and scientists from the National Museum of Nature and Science in Tsukuba, Japan, are also participating in the research.

It is a particular dinosaur because it was found in the south of Argentina, in the province of Santa Cruz, south of the city of Calafate." VARIOUS Matias Motta analysing fossil remains of Kank Australis SOT, Matias Motta, Palaeontologist (Spanish): "This dinosaur has several important features. Firstly, its age. It is about 70, 65 million years old. It is an age just before the extinction of the dinosaurs, of the large dinosaurs. So we are surveying a dinosaur, what its characteristics were, what its life was like just before the extinction of the dinosaurs in Patagonia, particularly." VARIOUS Matias Motta observing images on computer SOT, Matias Motta, Palaeontologist (Spanish): "This dinosaur is particular. It belongs to the unenlagiid group. A group of raptor dinosaurs that perhaps are more known in the northern hemisphere, such as the velociraptors, for example, which we have seen in many movies, but here in Argentina and South America there was a particular group of these raptor dinosaurs which we call unenlagiid and among them is the Kank Australis." M/S Matias Motta making notes M/S Matias Motta analysing fossil remains SOT, Matias Motta, Palaeontologist (Spanish): "This dinosaur, like other raptor dinosaurs, has the typical raptor claw. It is a very sharp curved claw that the index toe of the foot has. With that claw, it is believed they could hunt and would be active prey hunters. But this dinosaur like other unenlagiid dinosaurs. We believe it had an elongated snout with a well-elongated muzzle, loaded with many teeth, more than 20 teeth in the upper and lower parts. And these teeth were also particular because they were rather conical, different from other carnivorous dinosaurs that may have teeth more like a knife. In this case, this dinosaur had conical teeth with some striations that we believe would serve precisely to fish, so that the fish would not escape when catching them in the water." M/S Matias Motta analysing fossil remains C/U Claw of the Kank Australis SOT, Matias Motta, Palaeontologist (Spanish): "This dinosaur also found neck remains with these vertebrae we could determine that it had a quite mobile neck that reminds us a lot of the habit of storks or herons when fishing. So we are talking about a dinosaur that would live in a place of aquatic environments, like lagoons or rivers, a very different landscape from the current Patagonia, because it was a much more humid, temperate place, with seasonal rains. So in this environment lived the Khan Australis, probably fishing just like herons or storks do today." description: Self-taught chef Georgiana Viou, the first Black female chef in France to earn a Michelin star, said African cuisine is entering a new global moment as she champions the culinary traditions of her native Benin. 
Footage filmed on Monday in Cotonou shows Viou preparing a signature meat dish steeped in aromatic spice, demonstrating how traditional West African culinary foundations are re-centering global fine dining. 
"It is Africa's time. [...] There are many people, both women and men, working to promote African cuisines," she said in an exclusive interview. 
She noted that chefs, farmers, journalists, artisans, and food festivals are shifting the global culinary axis away from Eurocentric monopolies, bringing authentic visibility to the continent's diverse heritage. 
"All these movements, commitments and cooking help to raise awareness of the cuisines of the African continent. And I think that is a good sign," she explained. 
Born in Benin, Viou moved to France to study and later gained recognition after reaching the final stages of MasterChef France in 2008. She went on to open her own restaurant, publish cookbooks and receive a Michelin star in 2023. 
"I was self-taught also by necessity, and I never stopped learning. I had no other ambition than to be a nice cook," she recalled. 
Viou described her rise in French gastronomy as deeply personal, saying she had long felt like an outsider in the industry. 
"To see that entire room rise to its feet and applaud truly moved me. It felt like a form of healing," she said. 
"I'm doing this for my country. The media often refer to me as the Franco-Beninese chef, but I actually only hold a Beninese passport. I feel that I already have a country - and I am a citizen of that country," she concluded. 
Rejecting the industry's tendency to reduce Global South creators to a marketing trend, Viou remains committed to using her global platform as an instrument of national pride and cultural agency.

description: DRC's Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba said on Thursday that the first Ebola patient 'completely recovered' after two negative follow-up tests, as he sought to calm fears over the disease outbreak in the country. 
Speaking at a briefing in Bunia, the capital of Ituri province, Kamba said the patient was a female laboratory worker who had been infected and developed symptoms. 
"I am even happier to come the day after the confirmation of a case that has been declared recovered. She is now completely recovered after two negative follow-up tests," he stated. 
The minister said authorities continue to monitor the outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain, but stressed that the reported figure of 906 cases referred to 'suspected' cases, not confirmed infections. 
He said more than 648 tests were carried out in the latest reporting period, with 125 confirmed positive by laboratory testing, while 105 patients were currently being treated in healthcare facilities. 
"We cannot be told the epidemic is out of control when we have 105 cases that can be treated in a single referral hospital," he said. 
He also said the outbreak remained largely concentrated in Ituri province, with only 21 suspected cases recorded outside it - 20 in North Kivu and one in South Kivu. 
"This number should not make us paranoid enough to say we are in an uncontrolled epidemic," Kamba concluded. 
Ebola outbreak was declared by the DRC and Uganda on May 15, after laboratory tests confirmed Bundibugyo virus disease. WHO named it a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17.  
As of May 21, WHO said the DRC had reported 83 confirmed cases, including nine deaths, as well as 746 suspected cases and 176 suspected deaths. Later reporting put the toll at more than 900 suspected cases and around 220 suspected deaths.  
Uganda has temporarily closed its border with the DRC, with exceptions for Ebola response teams, humanitarian operations, cargo, food transport and security movements, all subject to strict screening.

description: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te visited troops at the Air Force Command Headquarters in Kaohsiung on Friday, where he spoke on cuts to the special defence budget, which he says has “undermined Taiwan’s defence self-reliance goals.”

"The version of the special defence budget passed at its third reading by the Legislative Yuan has left these production lines without the necessary funding, greatly undermining our defence self-reliance goals. Many critical and important military procurement budget items have been removed by the Legislative Yuan without justification, creating gaps in our air defence architecture," he said during an address at the base.

Taiwan’s legislature has passed an NT$8.81 billion special defence budget funded through government borrowing. 

The vote comes just days before a reported payment deadline for US High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS), which anchor the package alongside self-propelled howitzers, anti-armour drones, and two types of anti-tank missiles.

However, the final bill includes deep cuts that heavily impact domestic production.

To address these vulnerabilities, Lai announced that his administration will pursue supplementary budgets, regular annual budget increases, or dedicated special legislation to secure key areas such as air defence and unmanned vehicles. "We will sustain international cooperation, promote defence industry self-reliance, build an intelligent and sustainable national defence capability, and ensure the peace, stability, and status quo of the Taiwan Strait," Lai emphasised.

This fiscal friction coincides with mounting geopolitical pressures across the Strait.

Chinese President Xi Jinping recently issued a direct warning to US President Donald Trump, explicitly stating that the Taiwan question carries a severe risk of direct conflict between the United States and China if not managed with ‘extreme care’.

Taiwan, which China claims as its own territory, has vowed to defend its democratic way of life, turning these budgetary struggles into a critical test of the island’s long-term survival strategy.

video991
description: Russian para-climber Rustam Nabiev has become the first person in the world to conquer Mount Everest using only his arms.
Footage captured between May 14-20 shows Nabiev making his way up the highest peak on the planet - with his unique technique, using two axes. The video taken on Wednesday features relatives and close friends greeting the athlete at Ufa International Airport  - along with banners and traditional food.
"Thousands of people were on the route, thousands saw me ascending, and after my ascent they showed respect, admiration, and paid tribute to what I had done," Nabiev revealed.
The athlete revealed that his main motivation was the desire to 'return home' to his family.
"That was probably one of the most important goals, because reaching the summit is only 50 per cent of the task. The main task is descending safely, alive and healthy. I saw many people who died after reaching the summit, right before my eyes, so I know very well that I could have ended up in the same situation," the para-climber added.
Nabiev’s wife Indira Nabieva,admitted she prayed for her husband throughout the expedition.
"The scariest moments were during the summit push, during those final days of his ascent of Everest. There was a lot of anxiety, but I prayed, believed, and waited at home. <…> It’s about depth, about strength of spirit, about motivation - that the impossible is still possible," she emphasised.
The para-climber lost both legs in 2015 in a tragic accident during military service, when a barracks collapsed on him. He spent more than seven hours under the rubble before undergoing amputation.
The ascent of Everest, completed on May 20, was Nabiev’s tenth major climb. His first peak was Mount Elbrus, where he developed his unique ascent method. His achievements also include Manaslu, Ararat, Kazbek, Kilimanjaro, Aconcagua, Pik Lyubvi, and Mount Iremel.
Nabiev is planning to complete the Seven Summits programme - climbing the highest peaks of all continents. His next goal is Antarctica, with the expedition planned within the next six months.

description: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Mao Ning on Friday expressed Beijing's opposition to newly announced maritime border negotiations between the Philippines and Japan. The diplomatic friction comes as Tokyo and Manila elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership on Thursday and agreed to launch formal military intelligence-sharing talks. 
Speaking at a press briefing in Beijing, Mao raised concerns over the issue, calling it a 'grave violation of international law', particularly the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), noting that the maritime areas involved lie east of Taiwan, which China claims sovereignty over. 
"China solemnly declares that the so-called 'delimitation negotiations' by Japan and the Philippines are completely illegal and invalid, and will not affect China's claims to rights in the waters east of Taiwan Island or the exercise of its legitimate rights and interests," Mao said. 
"China urges Japan and the Philippines to immediately cease any actions that infringe upon China's maritime rights and interests," she continued. 
At the Tokyo Summit on Thursday, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr agreed to advance talks on the General Security of Military Information Agreement (GSOMIA) to enhance intelligence sharing among Indo-Pacific partners, while also accelerating discussions on economic and maritime cooperation. 
During the presser, Mao also cautioned against Japan's 'remilitarisation', noting reports that Defence Ministry orders have tripled in five years and made up half of public-demand government orders in fiscal 2025. 
"The Japanese government is continuously loosening restrictions and injecting funds into the defence industry through increased fiscal spending, institutional support, and the lifting of export controls [...] This runs counter to Japan's self-proclaimed image as a peace-loving nation," Mao noted. 
"Is Japan destined to repeat the mistakes of history and return to the path of militarist expansion? People of peace around the world, including the Japanese public, should remain highly vigilant," she warned. 
The spokesperson also urged the European Union to view its trade ties with China 'in a comprehensive and objective manner', amid reports that European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is seeking to curb subsidised Chinese imports. 
The EU's goods trade deficit with China widened from €312 billion in 2024 to €360 billion last year, and expanded further at a faster pace in the first quarter of 2026, according to reports.

video994
description: In the Rohingya refugee camps of Cox's Bazar, on the southeastern coast of Bangladesh, the community marked Eid al-Adha with communal prayers and a spirit of togetherness, despite the harsh conditions they face as refugees.

More than a million have sought shelter here after fleeing a brutal military crackdown in Myanmar, making it the world’s largest refugee camp.

Dressed in clothing donated or bought with limited funds, refugees filled makeshift mosques for prayers, performing ablutions before the Imam delivered his heartfelt sermon.

“In Islam, sacrificing an animal on the day of Eid al-Adha is the most rewardable act in the sight of Allah,” said Roshid Abul Kalam, a Rohingya Islamic teacher.

Post prayers, families flooded the camp’s streets, where children enjoyed snacks, toys, and games while mothers cooked Qurbani meat. Sharing a meal symbolises a small sense of normalcy amidst adversity.

Hasina, a Rohingya housewife, expressed gratitude, “Because my husband is suffering from a serious illness, we could not perform Qurbani this year. But the people around us were very kind — they shared their meat with us, and Alhamdulillah, I was able to feed my children fully.”

Bodorud Duja, a 70-year-old Rohingya refugee, shared his noble intention, “If Allah grants me the opportunity to perform Qurbani, I would divide the meat into three shares - one for the orphans, one for the poor, and one for my family.”

Despite the festive spirit, many struggled to perform Qurbani due to the hardships of refugee life. Nevertheless, the community's generosity ensured that no family was left without.

Eid al-Adha, known as the ‘Festival of Sacrifice’, commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah, and is celebrated globally through the ritual sacrifice of livestock and the sharing of meat with family, neighbours, and those in need.

video1000
description: Barcelona bookstore group Finestres has opened what organisers describe as the world’s first bookshop outside Palestine dedicated exclusively to Palestinian culture, thought and literature. 
Footage captured on Thursday shows visitors moving through the new venue, browsing displays of poetry, fiction, essays and political writing. 
The new Finestres Palestina space, located in Barcelona’s Gracia neighbourhood, has around 4,000 books in several languages. Organisers say the collection includes fiction, poetry, essays, art, theatre, children’s books and gastronomy, with a strong focus on Palestinian authors and perspectives. 
Olivia Watson, who heads the bookstore, said the aim was to go beyond headlines and offer a deeper understanding of Palestinian daily life. 
"Since 2023, lots of people who didn't know anything about the Palestinian context have seen what's happening in the headlines and are shocked by it. What that doesn't give people is a better understanding of the reality of Palestinian food, of Palestinian day-to-day reality, and that's what literature can do for us," Watson explained. 
"I think we need to, as a society, promote Palestinian voices at a time when they're being silenced. And that means proactively dedicating a space to Palestinian culture, Palestinian writing and literature, and trying to do our part to make sure that the genocide ends," she added. 
Watson said the response since opening had been strong, particularly from members of the Palestinian diaspora. 
"We opened less than two weeks ago, and hundreds of people have been through, especially people from the diaspora, have been really excited to have this space," she said. 
Palestinian literature has long explored themes of identity, displacement, memory and exile, with writers documenting both personal and political histories. 
Among the most influential voices is Edward Said, the Palestinian-American scholar whose work helped shape postcolonial studies, including his landmark book Orientalism. Poetry has also been central to Palestinian cultural expression, particularly the work of Mahmoud Darwish, often described as Palestine’s national poet. 
The opening comes amid the ongoing conflict in Gaza. The war escalated on October 7, 2023, after a Hamas-led attack on Israel killed 1,139 people and saw more than 200 hostages taken. 
Israel then launched a military campaign across Gaza. Palestinian health authorities say at least 72,803 people have been killed and more than 172,855 wounded. 
In January, US Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff announced the start of the second phase of the Trump administration’s 20-point Gaza plan, saying it would move from ceasefire to demilitarisation, technocratic governance and reconstruction. Palestinian officials have repeatedly accused Israel of violating the agreement.
